title: A reliably green baseline: fix the flaky download-queue tests
description: The first CI runs on the new repository (RomMix v0.20.0, unchanged) failed on a commit upstream's CI passed. x64 `npm test`: 'a transfer that cannot be resumed is not interrupted' and 'changing the order of the queue' (per-test temporary log and download folders removed while still in use: 'logging to file stopped: ENOENT ... /tmp/rommix-downloads-test-*/logs/app.log'). x64 `npm run test:app`: 15 s timeouts in 'pausing one stops it where it is, and it picks up from there', 'and cancelling throws it away rather than pausing it' and 'driving the queue from the activity tab'. arm64 `npm run package -- --arm64`: 'getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN github.com' while electron-builder fetched its assets. The branch ruleset needs a baseline that is green every time, so this is the first unit of work, before M0-01.
acceptance: A `workflow_dispatch` workflow `.github/workflows/stress.yml` (inputs: suite, runs, arch) runs `npm test` and `npm run test:app` back to back; the PR links runs showing 20 consecutive green runs of each on x64 and 10 on arm64.

Each fix addresses a root cause and the PR names it: a temporary folder outlives every handle on it (the file logger is stopped and awaited before the folder is removed); the fake server and the queue are awaited by state (an event, or a polled condition with a deadline), never by sleeping.
No test is skipped, marked todo, wrapped in a retry or quarantined, and no timeout is raised as the only change (the evaluator checks the diff for each).

The package step runs from cache: `~/.cache/electron` and `~/.cache/electron-builder` are restored with actions/cache keyed on package-lock.json, and a separate warm-up step fetches what is missing with at most 3 attempts and back-off; the packaging itself is never retried.
docs/PROGRESS.md records each flaky test, its root cause, the fix and the stress-run links. Dependabot PRs #1-#3 are triaged only after this merges (CLAUDE.md, rule 7).

title: Overlay bootstrap and upstream baseline
description: Confirm the handoff kit sits correctly on top of the RomMix v0.20.0 baseline: placeholders replaced, upstream agent skills removed, RomMix's own CLAUDE.md rules carried into the root CLAUDE.md, and the upstream base recorded.
acceptance: `grep -rn --exclude-dir=.git --exclude=HANDOFF.md --exclude=features.json '__GH_OWNER__\|__REPO__' .` prints nothing (those two files quote the placeholders on purpose).
`.claude/skills/`, `.agents/` and `skills-lock.json` do not exist (the upstream `update` skill commits straight to main).

`docs/UPSTREAM.md` records the upstream repo, the base commit (v0.20.0, ea787b98c32ce6efcd0c0448c0dac5aed074f3af), the commit studied for the plan (990e55e3855db5ef0c92324283664b71f14fd37d) and the rule for pulling upstream changes.
`npm ci && npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test` passes on the cloud VM with Node 24, and the output is pasted into the PR.

title: Agent scripts: init, check, next, and the Stop hook
description: Add `scripts/agent/init.sh` (idempotent: Node 24 check, `npm ci` when the lockfile changed, `npx install-electron`, Docker RomM up and provisioned, smoke test), `scripts/agent/check.sh` (format:check, lint, typecheck, test, coverage), `scripts/agent/next.mjs` (lists eligible features) and a Stop hook in `.claude/settings.json` that runs check.sh when tracked source changed.
acceptance: Running `scripts/agent/init.sh` twice in a row on a fresh cloud VM exits 0 both times; the second run takes under 90 s.
`scripts/agent/init.sh` fails with a clear message (not a stack trace) when Node is not 24.x, when Docker is unavailable, or when RomM never reports healthy.
`node scripts/agent/next.mjs` prints features whose `passes` is false and whose `depends_on` all pass, in milestone order, and marks the ones blocked by a gate.

`.claude/settings.json` registers a Stop hook that runs `scripts/agent/check.sh` only when `git diff --name-only origin/main` touches `src/`, `test/`, `packaging/`, `scripts/` or `native/`, and blocks the turn while it fails.
`.claude/settings.json` registers a SessionStart hook gated on `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true` that puts Node 24 first on PATH and prints the session ritual from CLAUDE.md.

`scripts/agent/init.sh` fetches `origin/device-results` and prints `node scripts/agent/device-results.mjs --summary` (or, before M0-23, the raw `results/latest.json` and `bridge/status.json`, or 'no device results yet').

title: Feature list guard
description: `scripts/agent/features-check.mjs` validates docs/features.json in CI: schema, unique ids, existing depends_on with no cycles, coverage of every REQ/PARITY/BEYOND item, that the only change to an existing feature in a PR is its `passes` flag, and that `passes` flips only with the evidence its verification type requires.
acceptance: The script fails CI when any feature object has a field other than id, milestone, title, description, source, acceptance, verification, depends_on, passes, or a verification other than `ci`, `agent-screenshot`, `device` or `acceptance`.
It fails when REQ-1..15, PARITY-1..48 or BEYOND-1..18 is missing from every `source` list, or when depends_on has a cycle.
On a pull request it compares against the base branch and fails if an existing feature's title, description, source, acceptance, verification or depends_on changed (new features may be appended).

A `device` feature may flip `passes` to true only when the PR's PROGRESS entry has `PASSES <id> device:<sha>`, `origin/device-results:results/<sha>/summary.json` shows every `Device check` id named in that feature's acceptance as `pass` together with `safety.owner-state` and `safety.server-readonly`, and the commit that added `READY-FOR-DEVICE <id>` to docs/PROGRESS.md is an ancestor of `<sha>`.
An `acceptance` feature may flip only with `PASSES <id> acceptance:<date>` and a pass for that id in `origin/device-results:acceptance/<date>/results.json`.
Every `Device check` id in features.json appears in the check catalogue in docs/TESTING.md, and every `device` feature names at least one.
Unit tests cover each rule with a fixture file.

title: Rebrand to the fork's own identity
description: Rename the product so it can sit beside stock RomMix on the same device: product name, appId, executable, AppImage and Steam-script names, home folder and its XDG pointer, updater endpoints and user-facing strings. Internal code identifiers (RomMixApp, ROMMIX_* variables) stay, to keep upstream merges cheap. The name comes from docs/decisions/0001-fork-rommix.md.
acceptance: `electron-builder.yml` produces `<Name>-arm64.AppImage` and `<Name>-x86_64.AppImage` with appId `io.github.<owner>.<Name>`; `packaging/rommix-steam.sh` is shipped as `<name>-steam.sh` and finds `<Name>-*.AppImage` beside it.

The default home folder is `~/<name>`, the XDG pointer is `~/.config/<name>/root` (src/main/root.ts) and Electron's profile folder is `~/.config/<Name>`; a unit test proves a machine holding stock RomMix's `~/rommix`, `~/.config/rommix/root` and `~/.config/rommix` profile (as the owner's Nova does after Phase 0) is left untouched.
`src/main/update.ts` reads releases and the rolling channel from this repository, derived from one constant; `grep -rn 'leclercb/rommix' src packaging scripts` finds only attribution comments.
Every user-facing occurrence of the old product name in `src/shared/i18n/*.ts` uses the new one, and `npm test` (catalog placeholder checks) passes.
README.md says this is a fork of RomMix, links upstream, keeps the MIT notice and names the original author.

`GALLEON_HOME` overrides the home folder and is read before the pointer file; `ROMMIX_HOME` is not read (the one `ROMMIX_*` variable that is renamed), so stock RomMix's environment can never point Galleon at RomMix's folder (unit test).

title: CI on both architectures, every gate inside the build job, within the time budget
description: Extend `.github/workflows/release.yml` so the `build` matrix job (x64 on ubuntu-24.04, arm64 on ubuntu-24.04-arm) runs every gate within the CI time budget in docs/PLAN.md section 4: expensive checks once on x64, build, package and a smoke test on arm64, path-filtered steps for the slow suites, caches for Electron and electron-builder. Required-check names stay `build (ubuntu-24.04, x64)` and `build (ubuntu-24.04-arm, arm64)`.
acceptance: The workflow name, the job id `build` and the matrix keys are unchanged, both legs have `timeout-minutes: 20`, and there is no job-level `if:` on `build` and no `continue-on-error` anywhere.

The x64 leg runs, in order: format:check, lint, typecheck, `npm run test:coverage` (floor from package.json: lines 96, branches 88, functions 89), features-check, the bridge unit tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/device-bridge`), the PR-body check, the licence guard, Docker RomM 5.2.0 `npm run test:romm` (and `test:saves` from M2) when the `changes` step reports client, save, sync or fixture changes, build, package (skipped only on docs-only pull requests), `npm run test:app`, and the pull-request subset of `shots:nova`.
The arm64 leg runs build, package (skipped only on docs-only pull requests) and `npm run smoke:app`: the packaged app starts under Xvfb against the fake server, reaches Home and quits within 60 s.

Step conditions use only `matrix.arch`, the outputs of one `changes` step (an inline `git diff --name-only` against the base, or dorny/paths-filter pinned by SHA) and the event name; on pushes to `main` packaging always runs on both legs.
Caches: npm through setup-node, and `~/.cache/electron` plus `~/.cache/electron-builder` keyed on package-lock.json; RomM and MariaDB images are pulled once per job by digest.

`concurrency` cancels superseded pull-request runs, and the median wall time per leg over the last 10 pull requests is at most 10 minutes (`node scripts/agent/ci-times.mjs` prints it from the check-runs API).
Screenshots and test:app failure captures are uploaded as artifacts named per architecture.
A deliberately failing unit test on a scratch branch turns the x64 required check red (verified once; the scratch PR is closed).

title: RomM 5.2.0 and 5.3.1 in Docker, provisioned without a person
description: Add `test/romm/compose.yml` (MariaDB on tmpfs plus pinned `rommapp/romm:5.2.0` and `:5.3.1`, metadata providers off) and `test/romm/provision.mjs`, a port of Grout's MIT provision flow: first admin while the setup wizard is active (CSRF cookie echoed), a quick scan over socket.io with `apis: []`, a client token, and a device. Also a headless device-pairing test.
acceptance: `docker compose -f test/romm/compose.yml --profile v520 up -d` then `node test/romm/provision.mjs --profile v520` leaves a server whose `GET /api/heartbeat` reports `SYSTEM.VERSION` 5.2.0, with the fixture platforms scanned, in under 4 minutes on the cloud VM.
The same works with `--profile v531` (5.3.1) and on the ubuntu-24.04-arm runner.
Provisioning writes `test/romm/.state/<profile>.json` (git-ignored) with base URL, admin user, client token and device id, and is idempotent.

A test pairs a device end to end: `POST /api/auth/device/init`, approval through `POST /api/auth/device/approve` as the admin, then `POST /api/auth/device/token` returns an access token and device id.
Grout's licence and the ported file are credited in THIRD_PARTY.md; no metadata provider is contacted (all API keys empty).

title: Fixture library that mirrors the owner's library shapes
description: Generate a synthetic library under `test/romm/library/` with the shapes in docs/DEVICE-FACTS.md (multi-disc PS1 and GameCube folders, PS2 cue/bin pairs listed separately, PSP folders with .EDAT extras, a PSP entry with no extension, Dreamcast .chd and .cdi, SNES and GBA files, firmware stubs) plus legally redistributable homebrew ROMs fetched by manifest with SHA-256 and licence.
acceptance: `node test/romm/make-library.mjs` builds the tree deterministically (same bytes every run); no commercial ROM or BIOS bytes are in the repository.
`test/fixtures/roms/manifest.json` lists each homebrew file with source URL, SHA-256, licence and attribution, and `scripts/agent/fetch-fixtures.mjs` refuses a file whose hash differs.

After a RomM scan the platforms ps1/psx, ps2, psp, ngc, dc, snes and gba exist and the multi-disc, cue/bin and nested-folder rows appear with the same `has_multiple_files` / `has_nested_single_file` flags as on the owner's server.
BIOS stubs are zero-filled files with the expected names (e.g. `scph5501.bin`, `dc_boot.bin`) and are never presented as real firmware.

title: Real-server integration suite (`npm run test:romm`)
description: Run the RomMix client (`src/main/romm/client.ts`, `transfer.ts`) against the Dockerized RomM for the calls the fork depends on: heartbeat, pairing, platforms, paged ROM listing with and without files, single-file download with Range resume, multi-file download, per-file download (`file_ids` and `/files/content/`), firmware, save and state upload/download, device registration, play sessions.
acceptance: `npm run test:romm` runs against 5.2.0 and 5.3.1 in sequence and exits non-zero on any failure.
A download interrupted at 50% resumes with `Range: bytes=<n>-` and the result matches the file's `md5_hash` from `files[]`.
The suite asserts `GET /api/roms/{id}/files/content/{name}` works with GET on 5.2.0 (Phase 0 saw 405 only for HEAD) and records the outcome in the test name.
Every request body sent is checked against the schema snapshot in `schema/` for that version.

title: 1280x960 screenshot harness the agent can read
description: Add `npm run shots:nova`: launch the built app under Xvfb at 1280x960 against the fake RomM in `test/app/server.ts`, walk every screen with the pad driver in `test/app/driver.ts`, and write PNGs plus a contact sheet. The agent inspects them with its image viewer; CI uploads them.
acceptance: `npm run shots:nova` writes `artifacts/shots/<screen>.png` at exactly 1280x960 for Home, Library, a game page (each tab), Downloads, BIOS, Emulators, Settings (each tab), the setup wizard and the running overlay.
It also writes `artifacts/shots/index.html` showing all screenshots with their names, and exits non-zero if any screen fails to load.
Screens are reached by walking with the pad, not by calling into the app, as `scripts/screenshots.mjs` already does.
Running it twice on the same commit gives images whose pixel difference is under 0.5% (ImageMagick `compare -metric AE`), so later golden tests are meaningful.
`npm run shots:nova -- --subset pr` covers Home, Library, a game page, Downloads, Settings and the setup wizard in at most 2 minutes on the x64 runner; the full set runs nightly (M0-24).

title: Frame-time overlay and performance log
description: A toggle (Settings -> System, and the chord L3+R3 held 2 s) shows a small overlay with frame time p50/p90/p99, the share of janky frames (>1.5x the display interval) and the current screen, measured from requestAnimationFrame. A summary per screen goes to the log and the diagnostics bundle.
acceptance: The overlay draws in a corner without changing layout and costs under 0.3 ms per frame (measured in a test:app scenario with the overlay on and off).
Statistics come from a pure module (`src/renderer/src/perf/frames.ts`) with unit tests for percentiles and the janky threshold at 60 Hz and 120 Hz.
With the overlay on, a 30 s scripted scroll of a 1,300-game platform in test:app logs `perf summary {screen, frames, p50, p90, p99, jankyPct}` to app.log.

The overlay also shows the power state read from sysfs without root: CPU governor and current/max frequency of the prime cluster (policy7), GPU devfreq governor and frequency, and the Armada profile from `/run/armada/perf-state.json` and `/usr/share/armada/power-profiles.conf` when readable (pure parser with fixture tests; 'unknown' when unreadable).
On the device (informational): device checks `grid.scroll@performance` and `grid.scroll@balanced` record the same statistics on the Nova through the self-test (M0-21).

title: Diagnostics bundle: Report a problem
description: Settings -> System -> Report a problem (and an entry in the quit dialog) writes `~/<name>/reports/<timestamp>.zip`: app and launcher logs, pre-flight results, redacted settings, versions (app, commit, channel, Electron, Chromium), OS release, kernel, Mesa and gamescope versions where readable, the relevant environment variables, emulator probe results, the last 5 launch commands and exits, the latest perf summaries, and the power state (CPU governors and frequencies per policy, GPU devfreq governor and frequency, Armada profile and per-app override when readable).
acceptance: Redaction is a pure function with unit tests: the RomM base URL host becomes `<server>`, any `rmm_` token, bearer header, password, cookie and pairing code is removed, and IPv4/IPv6 addresses become `<ip>`; a test feeds a log containing each and asserts none survive.
The bundle never includes `config/` credentials or keyring data (test asserts file list).
The zip is written with the existing `zipDirectory` in `src/main/zip.ts` and is under 20 MB (logs are tail-trimmed).
A test:app scenario presses Report a problem with the pad and finds the zip on disk.

title: Problem reports reach the agent without GitHub
description: The owner does not file GitHub issues. A Report a problem bundle (M0-11) saved in Galleon on the Nova is collected by the device bridge on its next run, sanitised again, and published under `reports/<time>/` on the `device-results` branch; the agent treats each new report as an owner-authored bug. The phone hand-off and the prefilled GitHub form of the earlier plan are dropped. The dialog says plainly that the report is picked up automatically the next night the Nova is charging in Game Mode.
acceptance: The dialog text (all four catalogues) says where the report is saved and that it is picked up automatically; no QR code or GitHub link is shown.
`scripts/agent/device-results.mjs` lists new `reports/` folders since the last session and opens one issue per report (labels `bug`, `device-report`), quoting only the sanitised summary.

Device check `report.bundle`: the self-test opens Report a problem with the internal pad driver; the bundle appears in the test home, holds no credentials (file list) and passes the bridge's sanitiser with nothing withheld.

title: Update channels with checksums
description: Keep upstream's rolling `canary` pre-release (built from every green push to main) as the in-app update channel, publish SHA256SUMS beside it, and make `<name>-steam.sh --canary` the documented way to stay on it. Updates are verified against the checksum before they are swapped in. The device bridge tests the separate `nightly` pre-release (M0-24), which adds the test bundle.
acceptance: Each push to main publishes or replaces the `canary` pre-release with both AppImages, the Steam script and `SHA256SUMS`, and moves the tag last (as `release.yml` already does).
The updater (`src/main/update.ts`) refuses an image whose SHA-256 does not match `SHA256SUMS`, logs why, and keeps the running version (unit test).
The footer and Settings -> About show version, short commit and channel.
Device check `build.identity`: the app under test reports the version and commit named in the nightly's `build-info.json`.

Device check `update.verify`: in the test home, the updater reads the live channel and its `SHA256SUMS`, accepts the matching image and refuses a deliberately corrupted copy, and replaces no installed AppImage.

title: Owner-gated stable releases from Actions
description: Add `.github/workflows/cut-release.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` with a version input, protected by the `release` environment (owner approval). It checks package.json and the CHANGELOG section, runs the same build matrix through a reusable workflow, creates the tag and release in the same run (tags made with the workflow token start no other workflow), and records the release.
acceptance: The release job cannot start until the owner approves the `release` environment.
It fails before tagging when package.json's version or the `## <version>` CHANGELOG section disagree with the input.
Building, tagging and publishing happen in one run, so no step depends on a tag-push trigger; the agent never pushes a tag.

After publishing, a PR appends the release to docs/PROGRESS.md. The owner approves the `release` environment, or the local Claude session does it on the owner's word during the acceptance session (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/pending_deployments`).

title: Acceptance backlog: one consolidated session script
description: `scripts/agent/acceptance.mjs` turns every `acceptance` feature whose code is merged (PROGRESS line `READY-FOR-ACCEPTANCE <id>`), plus every acceptance line marked informational, into `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`: one session script for the owner in plain words, grouped by where the owner is (the Nova in Game Mode, Android with Argosy, a browser), with a time estimate per group, a save backup first, and a results table the local Claude session fills in. It replaces the per-build checklists of the earlier plan.
acceptance: The generator is deterministic and unit-tested, and the session it writes totals at most two hours (the sum of the item estimates is checked).
Each item names the build, the exact menus and buttons, what success looks like, and the feature id it decides.
`acceptance/<date>/results.json` (schema in docs/TESTING.md) is read back by `scripts/agent/device-results.mjs`, which flips `passes` for items marked pass and opens a bug for each fail.
No item is something the device bridge can check; the evaluator rejects any that is.

title: Labels from the repository; owner issues without secrets
description: Add `.github/workflows/labels.yml` to sync labels from `.github/labels.yml`. There is no Routine API trigger and no repository secret: the Project and the hourly heartbeat Routine read owner-authored issues and the `device-results` branch at the start of every session. The `agent-dispatch.yml` of the earlier plan is not built.
acceptance: The label workflow creates or updates every label in `.github/labels.yml` and deletes none (crazy-max/ghaction-github-labeler pinned by SHA, `skip-delete: true`).
No workflow references `ROUTINE_FIRE_URL`, `ROUTINE_FIRE_TOKEN` or `TESTER_LOGIN` (features-check greps `.github/`).
CLAUDE.md's session ritual treats owner-authored open issues, and only those, as candidates for work.

title: One-line install and update from Desktop Mode
description: Add `install.sh` at the repo root: downloads the latest stable or nightly aarch64 AppImage and the Steam script from this repo's releases into `~/Applications`, verifies SHA-256, makes them executable, and writes `~/.local/share/applications/<name>.desktop` (Exec = the Steam script) so the app appears in Steam's 'Add a Non-Steam Game' program list. Phase 0 showed that list's Browse file picker never opens under KDE on the Nova, so the printed steps tick the app in the list and never use Browse. Re-running it updates in place. The local Claude session uses it to install Galleon for real during the acceptance session.
acceptance: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --nightly` works on a machine with only bash, curl, sha256sum and coreutils (shellcheck clean).
It refuses to install on a non-aarch64 machine unless `--arch x86_64` is given, and refuses a file whose checksum fails.
A CI test runs it on x64 with a fake HOME against a local fake releases API and checks the files, modes and an idempotent second run.
It never uses sudo and never writes outside `~/Applications` and `~/.local/share/applications`.
The `.desktop` entry passes `desktop-file-validate` and has Name, Icon (installed beside it) and `Categories=Game;`.
On the device (informational): device check `install.script` runs it into a throw-away HOME on the Nova.

title: Independent evaluator and pull-request discipline
description: Use `.claude/agents/evaluator.md` on every feature before merge, add `.github/pull_request_template.md` (feature ids, evidence, evaluator verdict, device checks added or changed, CI wall time per leg, risk), and document merging through REST after green checks.
acceptance: Every merged PR after this one contains an `Evaluator: PASS` section quoting the evaluator's findings, and a `Feature: <id>` line.
The PR template exists and CI fails a PR whose body lacks a `Feature:` line (simple workflow step in the build job).
docs/PROGRESS.md has one entry per session from here on (checked by features-check: an entry dated within the PR's lifetime).
PROGRESS entries record each PR's CI wall time per leg (from `node scripts/agent/ci-times.mjs <pr>`).

title: Watch upstream RomMix
description: A weekly workflow compares this repo's recorded upstream base with leclercb/rommix main via REST and opens or updates one issue `upstream: N new commits` listing subjects, so useful fixes (for example the controller-listing commits after v0.20.0) are ported deliberately.
acceptance: The issue lists commits since the base recorded in docs/UPSTREAM.md, with links, and is updated rather than duplicated.
The workflow only reads the public upstream API with the workflow token and never pushes.

title: Licence and dependency guard
description: Add `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` and a CI step that lists production dependency licences, fails on GPL/AGPL/LGPL in anything bundled into the AppImage, and greps the tree for text copied from GPL projects (Argosy, Tender, OpenGamepadUI, Ludo, ROCKNIX) by known identifiers.
acceptance: CI fails when a new runtime dependency is added without a DEPENDENCIES.md entry (name, exact version, licence, why).
CI fails on a GPL-family licence in the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all` plus licence metadata).
THIRD_PARTY.md lists MIT/MPL sources whose code or data is used (Grout, ES-DE data files, fonts) with licence text.

title: Self-test mode: scripted scenarios on the device, read-only towards RomM
description: When `GALLEON_HOME` is set and `$GALLEON_HOME/self-test-request.json` exists at start-up, Galleon takes the request (renames it so a restart does not repeat it), runs the scenarios it lists, driven from inside the app (its own pad-event driver and IPC, never OS input injection), writes `summary.json` to the results folder the request names, and quits with code 0. Scenarios: cold start-up time; a scroll of a 1,000+ game grid (the largest platform in the library, or a built-in synthetic 1,300-game platform without a server) with requestAnimationFrame frame-time capture (p50, p95, p99, frames, dropped frames above 1.5x the display interval), once per power profile in the request, with governor, clocks and Armada profile sampled during the scroll (`/usr/share/armada/power-profiles.conf`, `armada-power status`, cpufreq and devfreq sysfs); heartbeat and auth; a small ROM download with progress events; launch and graceful exit through each installed emulator with a bundled homebrew payload, checking that the emulator process and its window appeared (gamescope's focused-app and window-list atoms or the X11 window list; `gamescopectl screenshot` when present) and that it exited with code 0 within the grace period; self-screenshots with `webContents.capturePage` at 1280x960; and every feature check id the request names (catalogue in docs/TESTING.md). The safety rules are built into the app, not left to the harness.
acceptance: With `GALLEON_HOME` set, everything stays under it, including Electron's userData (profile, caches, single-instance lock); `~/.config/galleon/root`, the default home and stock RomMix's folders are never read or written (unit test with a fake home).

Read-only server guard: in self-test mode the RomM client refuses every method other than GET and HEAD before it reaches the network, strips `device_id` from save and state requests, never registers a device, never refreshes a token, and sends no play sessions or now-playing updates; each refusal is counted in `safety.serverWritesAttempted` (unit tests over every call site in `src/main/romm/client.ts` and `devices.ts`).
Privacy mode: no screen draws the server address, the account name or a pairing code while the self-test runs (test:app renders every screen with privacy on and searches the DOM).

Emulator sandbox: each emulator the self-test starts gets its own config, data and save folders under the test home (XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, Dolphin `-u`, RetroArch `--config` plus an appended config naming the sandbox's folders, flatpaks through `flatpak run --env=... --filesystem=<test home>`), with BIOS files linked read-only from the owner's folders; an emulator that cannot be sandboxed is skipped with reason `cannot-sandbox` and never run against the owner's folders (descriptor-level unit tests).

Abort on input: a button press or stick movement from the real controller stops the self-test within one second, writes `status: aborted-by-user` and quits, so run.sh can exit 20 (test:app with a simulated real pad).

`summary.json` follows the schema in docs/TESTING.md (a schema test), lists every requested check with result pass, fail, skip or error, its metrics, thresholds and evidence paths, and is written even when a scenario throws.
Device check `selftest.complete`: the start-up, grid-scroll and screenshot scenarios complete on the Nova and the app quits with code 0.
Device check `safety.server-readonly`: the run sent no request other than GET or HEAD to the RomM server and no save or state request with a `device_id`.
Device check `server.heartbeat`: with the imported sign-in, GET /api/heartbeat and GET /api/users/me succeed and the server version is recorded.
Device check `download.small`: the smallest SNES or GBA title downloads into the test home with progress events and a verified hash, and is deleted afterwards.
A self-test instance never writes Galleon's idle state file (M1-17), so the device bridge cannot mistake it for the owner's Galleon.

title: Device test bundle: run.sh, the test shortcut and owner-state protection
description: Build `galleon-device-tests.tar.gz` from `test/device/` in the nightly (M0-24): `run.sh` (entry point, POSIX sh), `bundle.json` ({contract, minBridge}), `thresholds.json`, `launch.sh`, Python 3 standard-library helpers (Steam CEF client, shortcuts.vdf reader, owner-state manifest, sanitiser rules shared with the bridge), the homebrew payloads from the M0-07 manifest with their licences, and `bridge/` (a copy of tools/device-bridge for its self-update). run.sh implements the contract in docs/PLAN.md section 5: a separate home, a read-only sign-in import, the owner-state manifest and restore, the 'Galleon Device Test' Steam shortcut, launch through `steam://rungameid/<gameid>` (fallback: the Steam CEF `SteamClient.Apps.RunGame`), the power-profile handshake through `armada-power`, audio muted and restored, a clean exit, and `--cleanup`.
acceptance: `run.sh` and `launch.sh` are shellcheck-clean, and the helpers have unit tests that run in CI, including a full dry run against a fake HOME, a fake `/sys/class/power_supply`, a fake Steam CEF endpoint and a fake `armada-power`.

The owner-state manifest covers stock RomMix's and the owner's Galleon config and credentials, every emulator save, memory-card and config folder in docs/DEVICE-FACTS.md, and Steam's shortcuts.vdf files; run.sh backs up the emulator config files before starting anything, restores any that changed, and fails `safety.owner-state` if the manifest taken after differs (test with a fake HOME where an emulator rewrites its config).

The sign-in import is read-only and ordered: the bridge's read-only token file, then the owner's Galleon config, then stock RomMix (`~/.config/rommix/root` or `~/rommix`; `config/settings.json` `server.baseUrl`; `config/credentials.bin` with magic `RAW1`). `ENC1` or nothing found skips the server checks with reason `no-importable-credentials`. The test home gets save sync up and down off, play sessions off, the guard on, and no device id (unit tests on fixtures).

Only small ROMs are downloaded (the smallest SNES and GBA titles, at most 16 MB each; anything else only as a capped Range read), only into the test home, and all are deleted before exit (test asserts the folder is empty).

Before launching, run.sh mutes the default audio sink and stops an idle owner's Galleon through its core socket; afterwards it restores the volume, the power profile and the owner's Galleon (relaunched through its own Steam shortcut) (tests with fakes).
Device check `harness.run`: run.sh finishes within the budget, the summary is complete and the device is back at Steam's library.
Device check `safety.owner-state`: the manifest taken after the run equals the one taken before.
Both checks pass on the Nova in two consecutive nightly runs, and the 'Galleon Device Test' shortcut does nothing when started by hand.

title: Device results drive the plan: ingestion and passes
description: `scripts/agent/device-results.mjs` fetches `origin/device-results` and reads `results/index.json`, `bridge/status.json`, and new `reports/` and `acceptance/` folders since the last ingested result (PROGRESS line `DEVICE-RESULTS <sha> <status>`). It maps check ids to features through the `Device check` lines in features.json and prints, in this order: safety failures, checks that newly fail (regressions), checks that newly pass with the features they complete, new problem reports, and how long ago the bridge was last seen. With `--apply` it flips `passes` under the rules of M0-03, sets `passes` back to false for a device feature whose check fails on a newer build, and opens one `regression` issue per such feature.
acceptance: Unit tests with fixture branches: a flip happens only when the feature's READY-FOR-DEVICE commit is an ancestor of the tested sha; a safety failure blocks every flip from that run; a later failure reverts the flip and opens exactly one regression issue; a `withheld`, `error` or `skipped` summary flips nothing.
The script has no code path that writes to `device-results` (a test greps for push commands).
It finishes in under 10 seconds on the cloud VM with a 60-result branch.
Its `--summary` output is the first thing CLAUDE.md's session ritual reads.

title: Nightly: heavy suites, the device test bundle and the nightly pre-release
description: Add `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (a daily schedule at an off-hour UTC time plus `workflow_dispatch`; its first step ends the run early when `main` has not moved since the last nightly). On both architectures it runs the full `npm run test:coverage`, the full `test:app`, the Docker RomM matrix (5.2.0 and 5.3.1, `test:romm` and, from M2, `test:saves`) and every screen of `shots:nova`; then it builds the device test bundle and publishes a rolling `nightly` pre-release with `Galleon-arm64.AppImage`, `Galleon-x86_64.AppImage`, `galleon-device-tests.tar.gz`, `build-info.json` ({sha, version, builtAt, bundleContract}) and `SHA256SUMS` covering all of them, moving the `nightly` tag last as release.yml does for `canary`. This is what the device bridge tests.
acceptance: Every job has `timeout-minutes: 30` and the workflow has `concurrency: {group: nightly, cancel-in-progress: false}`, so nightlies never stack; a typical run takes at most 30 minutes.
`build-info.json` names the exact commit built, `SHA256SUMS` covers every asset, and the `nightly` tag moves only after every asset is uploaded.
A failing suite fails the nightly and publishes nothing; the agent treats a red nightly like a red required check.
Until M0-22 lands, the bundle holds a minimal run.sh that writes a summary with only `harness.run`, so the bridge path is exercised end to end from the first nightly.
The pre-release is never marked latest, and its body says it exists for the device bridge.

title: Close Gate 0 on the record
description: Phase 0 (stock RomMix v0.20.0 on the Nova, Desktop and Game Mode) passed on 2026-10-08; the results were written into docs/PLAN.md and docs/TESTING.md at handoff. Open a `gate` issue that records the Gate 0 decision (proceed with the RomMix fork) and lists every Phase 0 caveat with the feature that addresses it, so the decision is traceable on GitHub.
acceptance: The `gate` issue quotes the PHASE 0 RESULTS table, states 'Gate 0: PASS, proceed with the fork', and is closed with a link from docs/PLAN.md.
Every caveat in PLAN.md's Phase 0 caveat list maps to a feature id that exists in docs/features.json (features-check verifies the list in PLAN.md).

title: DuckStation descriptor (Armada AppImage)
description: Add `src/config/emulators/duckstation/index.ts`: AppImage `~/Applications/DuckStation*.AppImage` (flatpak `org.duckstation.DuckStation` as a second route), systems `psx`, launch `-batch -fullscreen -nogui -- <rom>`, BIOS `~/.local/share/duckstation/bios`, saves `~/.local/share/duckstation/memcards` (per-game cards, `.mcd`).
acceptance: Registry and savepaths tests (`src/config/emulators/registry.test.ts`, `savepaths.test.ts`) cover install detection, argv for a .chd and an .m3u, and the save location.
No code outside `src/config/` names DuckStation (`grep -rn -i duckstation src --include=*.ts | grep -v src/config` is empty apart from i18n).
The descriptor's comments cite the flags' source (duckstation qthost.cpp at the pinned commit in docs/research/armada_integration.md).

title: ARMSX2 descriptor (Armada AppImage)
description: Add an ARMSX2 descriptor: AppImage `~/Applications/ARMSX2*.AppImage`, system `ps2`, launch `-batch -fullscreen -nogui -- <iso>`, BIOS `~/.config/ARMSX2/bios`, memory cards `~/.config/ARMSX2/memcards`, config `~/.config/ARMSX2/inis/PCSX2.ini`. Cue/bin rows launch the `.bin` because Armada's ps2 override rejects `.cue`.
acceptance: Tests cover argv for an .iso, a .chd and a cue/bin pair (the .bin is passed).
Saves are declared as `shared` until M2 adds folder-card handling, with a catalogue reason shown on the Saves tab.

Device check `launch.armsx2`: ARMSX2 starts the bundled PS2 payload fullscreen in its sandbox with no setup window, and its window takes focus (skipped with reason `missing-bios` when the Nova has no PS2 BIOS).

title: Dolphin descriptor (flatpak)
description: Add a Dolphin descriptor: flatpak `org.DolphinEmu.dolphin-emu`, systems `gc` and `wii`, launch `-b -C Dolphin.Display.Fullscreen=True -e <rom>` (verify the -C key against Dolphin source and record it), saves under `~/.var/app/org.DolphinEmu.dolphin-emu/data/dolphin-emu/GC` and `.../Wii/title`, states `.../StateSaves`.
acceptance: Tests cover argv for .iso, .rvz and a two-disc GameCube .m3u.
The -C key is verified in Dolphin's source at a pinned commit and cited in a comment.
Device check `launch.dolphin`: Dolphin starts the bundled GameCube homebrew `.dol` fullscreen in a sandbox user folder (`-u`), with no Dolphin main window.

title: PPSSPP descriptor (flatpak)
description: Add a PPSSPP descriptor: flatpak `org.ppsspp.PPSSPP`, system `psp`, launch `--fullscreen --pause-menu-exit <rom>`, saves `~/.var/app/org.ppsspp.PPSSPP/config/ppsspp/PSP/SAVEDATA` (directory per game), states `.../PSP/PPSSPP_STATE`.
acceptance: Tests cover argv for .iso, .cso and a nested-folder PSP row (the inner image is passed).
Device check `launch.ppsspp`: PPSSPP starts the bundled PSP homebrew fullscreen in its sandbox, and the stop path returns to Galleon.

title: Flycast descriptor (flatpak)
description: Add a Flycast descriptor: flatpak `org.flycast.Flycast`, system `dreamcast`, launch `<rom>` (exits on close when started from the command line), BIOS and VMUs in `~/.var/app/org.flycast.Flycast/data/flycast` (`dc_boot.bin`, `dc_flash.bin`).
acceptance: Tests cover argv for .chd, .cdi and .gdi.
BIOS placement puts `dc_boot.bin` and `dc_flash.bin` in the data folder (bios test).
Device check `launch.flycast`: Flycast boots the bundled Dreamcast homebrew fullscreen in its sandbox (its HLE BIOS when the real one is missing).

title: melonDS descriptor (Armada AppImage)
description: Add a melonDS descriptor: AppImage `~/Applications/melonDS*.AppImage`, system `nds`, launch `-f <rom>`, saves beside the ROM (Armada's template leaves SaveFilePath empty) declared as `perRom` in the ROM folder, config `~/.config/melonDS/melonDS.toml`.
acceptance: Tests cover argv and that save discovery looks next to the ROM.
Device check `launch.melonds`: melonDS opens the bundled NDS homebrew fullscreen, and a save written beside the ROM in the sandbox is found by save discovery.

title: RetroArch as Armada installs it
description: Adapt the existing RetroArch descriptor (`src/config/emulators/retroarch/index.ts`) for Armada: flatpak core folder, `--appendconfig=<launcher-owned cfg>` with `quit_on_close_content = "2"`, buildbot `linux/aarch64` cores, and launch variants per system for the Android-matching cores (snes9x, mgba, pcsx_rearmed, swanstation, beetle psx hw, ppsspp, dolphin, flycast) so the per-system choice of M2-08 can be honoured.
acceptance: The appended config file lives in the launcher's home, never edits `retroarch.cfg`, and is covered by a snapshot test.
Variants list only cores that RetroArch can load on aarch64 Linux (checked against the buildbot index in a test fixture).

Device check `launch.retroarch`: the RetroArch flatpak opens the bundled SNES homebrew fullscreen with the launcher-owned appended config, and Close Content returns to Galleon (`exit.retroarch`), leaving an `.srm` in the sandbox's save folder.

title: ES-DE find rules decide where emulators live
description: Add `src/main/findrules.ts`: read a vendored, pinned copy of ES-DE's `linuxarm` es_find_rules.xml and es_systems.xml (MIT, credited), layer Armada's `~/ES-DE/custom_systems/` overrides on top (an entry there replaces the bundled one by name), and resolve systempath/staticpath globs so descriptors' install routes find what the Armada Store installed.
acceptance: The parser keeps sibling elements outside the root (ES-DE files are not single-rooted) and has tests for override-by-name.
Resolution expands `~` and `*` and reports the first existing match; a test with a fake home holding `~/Applications/DuckStation-arm64.AppImage` resolves DuckStation.
The pre-flight check names the rule that found each emulator.

title: Library on the SD card by default
description: Phase 0 put a 1.46 GB GameCube download in `~/rommix/roms/gc/` on internal storage; the owner wants games on the SD card. Add a storage-location setting whose default is the ext4 SD card when one is mounted (`/run/media/<user>/<label>`, preferring label `NovaSD`), falling back to internal storage. Check the folder is writable and that flatpak emulators can read it (Armada grants `/run/media`). Keep BIOS and saves where emulators expect them. Handle the card being absent or unmounted without losing track of games.
acceptance: A pure module picks the default root from a volume list (unit tests: ext4 card present, card absent, card read-only, card nearly full, card present but not ext4, two cards).

When the chosen card is not mounted, games on it show 'card not inserted' instead of 'not downloaded', are never offered for re-download or pruned from the index (`Store.pruneInstalled` skips unmounted roots), and queued downloads wait with a clear message instead of falling back to internal storage silently.
Changing the ROM folder moves nothing silently: the app offers to move existing games and shows sizes first; Phase 0's games in `~/rommix/roms` can be adopted or moved.
Pre-flight shows the volume, file system and free space.

Device check `storage.sdcard`: with the card mounted, a fresh test home picks the mounted ext4 card (`/run/media/<user>/NovaSD`) as its default library root and `download.small` lands there and is deleted afterwards; with the root pointed at a simulated unmounted card, games show 'card not inserted' and nothing is pruned.

title: Hold Start to leave any emulator, with the save intact
description: Phase 0 proved RomMix's own exit works in Game Mode under Steam Input and InputPlumber: holding Start about 1.5 s (`SUSPENDED_HOLD_MS` in `src/renderer/src/input/gamepad.ts`) stopped RetroArch (flatpak) gracefully in about 300 ms through `stopFlatpakApp` in `src/main/host.ts`, and focus came back. Keep that mechanism. Harden it for every Armada emulator: exactly one SIGTERM per process, then automatic SIGKILL after the grace period for AppImage and native emulators too (today only flatpaks escalate on their own, and the force-close button cannot be seen while the emulator has the screen), only tracked processes signalled, never the launcher's own Steam scope. Then prove each emulator writes its save on that SIGTERM.
acceptance: The stop path (`askToQuit` in `src/main/launcher.ts`, `signalProcessGroup` and `stopFlatpakApp` in `src/main/host.ts`) is unit-tested with a fake process table: one SIGTERM per pid, SIGKILL only after the grace period, flatpak SIGTERM to the sandbox's processes before `flatpak kill`, and nothing outside the spawned tree is signalled.
The automatic escalation after a hold-to-exit is logged with the emulator, the grace used and whether the save directory changed during the grace period.
A test:app scenario holds Start on the stand-in emulator that ignores SIGTERM and sees it killed after the grace period with the session still reported.

Device check `exit.retroarch`, device check `exit.duckstation`, device check `exit.armsx2`, device check `exit.dolphin`, device check `exit.ppsspp` and device check `exit.flycast`: for each, the graceful stop (the path holding Start uses) ends the emulator with exit code 0, Galleon has focus again within 6 s (`focus.return`), no SIGKILL was needed, and where the payload writes a save the sandbox's save folder changed before the process ended.

title: Emulators start with a clean environment, inside Steam's tree
description: In `src/main/launcher.ts`, build each child's environment explicitly: drop Steam's overlay `LD_PRELOAD`, the AppImage runtime's `APPDIR`/`APPIMAGE`/`ARGV0`/`OWD` and any `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` it added, put `/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/bin` first on PATH (as `armada-game-launch` does), keep display and Steam variables, and keep spawning as a descendant (no double fork, no systemd-run).
acceptance: A pure `childEnvironment(parentEnv, descriptorEnv)` function has unit tests for each rule.
A test asserts the spawned process's parent chain leads back to the launcher (it is not reparented to init).
The exact environment differences are logged once per launch at debug level.

title: Nothing steals focus while a game runs
description: While an emulator or Steam game has the screen: never open a new top-level window (no toasts, no dialogs, no devtools), stop requestAnimationFrame-driven work and polling in the renderer, and after the emulator exits re-focus and redraw the launcher window once.
acceptance: A test:app scenario counts BrowserWindow instances and asserts no new window appears during a launch, including when a download finishes mid-game.
Notifications raised during play are queued and shown after the game ends (test).
Renderer frame callbacks drop to zero while suspended (measured via the perf module in test:app).
Device check `focus.no-new-window`: a download finishing while the sandboxed emulator has the screen opens no window (the window list is unchanged), and its notice appears after the exit.
Device check `focus.return`: after every emulator exit in the run, Galleon is the focused app again.

title: Steam games: list installed and launch
description: Add `src/main/steam/` (data parsing is emulator-agnostic, so it lives in main): read `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf` (and `config/libraryfolders.vdf`), each library's `appmanifest_*.acf` (appid, name, StateFlags, SizeOnDisk), show installed games (StateFlags & 4) as a 'Steam' platform, and launch with `/usr/bin/steam steam://rungameid/<appid>` using the clean environment.
acceptance: The text-VDF parser has tests built from real-shaped fixtures, including SD-card libraries under `/run/media` and partially installed games (excluded).
Launching logs the command and does not wait on Steam's process; the running overlay shows 'Playing on Steam'.
Device check `steam.list`: installed Steam games and non-Steam shortcuts are listed (counts and art found are published, never names).

Device check `steam.launch`: Galleon starts the 'Galleon Device Test Target' shortcut through `steam://rungameid/`; the result records whether it started, whether Steam showed 'Launch Multiple Games', and whether Galleon survived. A prompt left on screen marks the check `needs-attended`, and it is never run unattended again.

title: Usable at 1280x960 before the redesign
description: Make every inherited screen fit the Nova's 4:3 1280x960 panel with no clipped, overlapping or unreachable controls: a 4:3 layout profile chosen automatically by aspect ratio and size (Settings -> Interface -> Scale still overrides), and text no smaller than the RomMix default at that size.
acceptance: `npm run shots:nova` shows no element outside the viewport and no overlap on any screen (an automated bounding-box check in test:app reports offenders by data-* handle).
Every control on every screen is reachable with the d-pad (test:app walks each screen and visits every `data-action`).
The agent reviews the contact sheet and lists any visual defect in the PR.

title: Know the power profile, and tell the player
description: Phase 0 measured the cause of Game Mode lag: Armada's default Balanced profile (conservative governor, prime core capped near 2.09 GHz, GPU 220-680 MHz); with Performance the UI was as smooth as Desktop Mode, and Chromium was hardware-accelerated (Mesa through GLX on /dev/dri/renderD128). Read the power state without root, show a one-time hint when the launcher runs on Balanced or Eco ('for smoother browsing, set Performance for this app: Quick Access -> Armada Control'), and document that step in the player docs (M8-05). Armada keys per-game profiles by Steam appid, so every emulator the launcher starts inherits the launcher's profile.
acceptance: A pure parser reads `/usr/share/armada/power-profiles.conf`, `/run/armada/perf-state.json`, `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy*/scaling_{governor,cur_freq,max_freq}` and `/sys/class/devfreq/*/{governor,cur_freq}`; fixture tests cover balanced, performance, a missing file and an unknown format.
The hint appears at most once per profile change, can be dismissed for good, never appears outside Armada, and never tries to change the profile itself (the profile state is root-owned).
Pre-flight shows the current profile, governor and clocks.
Device check `power.read`: the profile, governor and clocks Galleon reads match `armada-power status` and sysfs under both profiles the harness sets.
Device check `power.hint`: the hint shows on Balanced and not on Performance (screenshots).

title: Core control socket
description: Expose a local JSON-lines socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<name>/core.sock` (mode 0600) from the main process with: status (connection, running game, downloads with progress, pending save uploads), quit-emulator, and pause/resume downloads. Document it in `docs/core-socket.md`. It is the boundary the Decky panel uses and the one a fallback UI would talk to.
acceptance: Protocol messages are typed in `src/shared/types/` and covered by unit tests, including malformed input.
The socket refuses connections from other users (file mode and SO_PEERCRED check) and is removed on exit.
A test drives quit-emulator through the socket and sees the same graceful stop path as holding Start.

The main process keeps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<name>/state.json` current (at least every 30 s; schema 1: `idle`, `steamAppId`, `updatedAt`), with `idle` true only while no game runs, no download is active and no save upload is pending; the device bridge reads it to tell an idle Galleon from someone playing (unit tests for each state).
The socket also accepts `quit-app`, which quits Galleon only when it is idle and answers why not otherwise (used by the device tests to hand the screen over politely).

title: Download progress with speed, time left and a cancel button
description: Add speed and time-left to the download engine (`src/main/downloads.ts`): an exponential moving average over 500 ms samples, time left from the smoothed speed, 'waiting for server' while RomM builds a zip, and a controller binding (X) that cancels the focused transfer from the Downloads screen and from a game page.
acceptance: The smoothing is a pure function with tests: constant rate converges within 3 s, a stall shows 'stalled' rather than a huge time left, and the estimate never flickers between units on steady input.
Download rows read like '15% - 613.6 MB / 3.8 GB - 41.4 MB/s - 1m 20s left' (format tested in all four catalogues).
Cancel removes the `.part` file and the queue row and is reachable with the pad (test:app).

Device check `download.progress`: a capped Range download (at most 400 MB) of the smallest ROM over 500 MB shows a speed and time left within 20% of the measured rate after the first 3 s, X on the internal pad driver cancels it, and its `.part` file is gone.

title: BIOS placement for Armada's emulators
description: Give each Armada descriptor its BIOS answer (`bios` field) so the existing BIOS screen copies RomM's firmware where each emulator reads it: DuckStation `~/.local/share/duckstation/bios`, ARMSX2 `~/.config/ARMSX2/bios`, Flycast data folder, RetroArch `system/`. Hash-verified, refusing unverified files unless the user confirms.
acceptance: `src/config/emulators/bios.test.ts` covers each target folder and the verified/unverified paths.

Device check `bios.targets`: every BIOS target folder resolves, present and missing files are reported by reading the owner's folders only, and installing a fixture BIOS into the sandbox puts it where the sandboxed emulator finds it.

title: Gate 1, decided by the device bridge
description: Gate 1 is decided by measurements from the device bridge, not by a person. Once every feature it depends on is READY-FOR-DEVICE, the agent evaluates the newest complete nightly results against the thresholds in docs/PLAN.md section 9 (data in `test/device/thresholds.json`) and records the outcome in PLAN.md and a closed `gate` issue. A smoothness or focus failure leads to documented optimisation rounds first, and only then to a pivot decision with a safe default.
acceptance: `node scripts/agent/gate1.mjs` reads the newest complete results and prints G1-1..G1-5 as pass or fail with the numbers; its rules are unit-tested on fixture summaries, including a run where only one power profile was measured (incomplete, not pass).
Gate 1 passes only when two consecutive complete nightly results each pass every criterion; their links are recorded in PLAN.md.

If G1-2 or G1-4 fails: at least two optimisation rounds, each a merged PR with before-and-after device numbers, are in PROGRESS.md before a `gate` + `needs-human` issue proposes the Godot pivot; the issue states the safe default (keep Electron and keep optimising), which the agent adopts in an ADR after 72 hours without an answer.
Device check `gate1.summary`: `gate1.mjs` run against the newest result reports every criterion as measured (no criterion missing data).

title: Server address without a scheme: try https, then http
description: Phase 0: a LAN address typed without a scheme was turned into https:// by `normaliseUrl` in `src/main/romm/client.ts`; the owner's RomM is plain http on a non-default port, so every attempt failed with 'fetch failed' until http:// was typed. When no scheme is typed, probe `https://` then `http://` with `GET /api/heartbeat`, keep the one that answers like RomM, show which one connected, and make errors specific.
acceptance: Unit tests with a fake transport: https answers -> https kept; https fails, http answers -> http kept and shown as 'Connected over http (not encrypted)'; both fail -> one message naming both attempts; an explicit scheme is never changed.
Error text distinguishes 'server answered on http but not https', 'nothing answered at this address', 'answered but is not RomM', and a TLS certificate problem, in all four catalogues.
The address saved is the one that worked, with its scheme, so later starts do not probe again; a later TLS failure is never silently downgraded to http.
Device check `server.scheme-probe`: given the imported address without its scheme, Galleon finds the scheme that answers like RomM and reaches the heartbeat with GET requests only.

title: Pairing that is easy to approve
description: Phase 0: approving through the login redirect link (`/login?next=/pair/device?user_code=...`) was confusing; approving from a browser already signed in to RomM, at `/pair/device?user_code=...`, worked. Show the QR code, the plain user code in large type, and the short direct URL `<server>/pair/device?user_code=<code>`, with the instruction to open it in a browser where you are already signed in to RomM. Keep polling with RFC 8628 back-off.
acceptance: The QR encodes the direct `/pair/device?user_code=` URL built from `verification_path_complete`, not a login redirect (unit test on the URL builder with 5.2.0-shaped responses).
The screen shows code, URL and instruction together at 1280x960 without scrolling (screenshot in `shots:nova`).
Polling honours `interval`, adds 5 s on `slow_down`, stops on `access_denied` or `expired_token` with a clear message and a 'get a new code' button (unit tests).
Device check `pairing.screen`: fed a fake code without calling the server, the pairing screen shows code, QR and URL together at 1280x960 without scrolling (screenshot).

title: Armada's emulator set, found as Armada installs it
description: Phase 0 found only RetroArch; it listed RetroDECK, EmuDeck, Eden and shadPS4 as missing and warned 'Flathub is not set up for your user' although Armada's flatpaks are system installs. Order the registry for armadaOS (Armada descriptors first), hide x86_64-only entries on aarch64 (RetroDECK is x86_64-only on Flathub), and make the pre-flight accept system-wide flatpak installs, asking for a user Flathub remote only when the user presses Install.
acceptance: `EMULATORS` order in `src/config/emulators/index.ts` puts the Armada descriptors before the upstream frontends, and an architecture filter hides descriptors whose every install route is unavailable on aarch64 (tests for both architectures).
Pre-flight treats an app found by `flatpak info --system <id>` as installed and shows no Flathub warning when nothing needs installing (unit test on parsed output).
`npm run shots:nova` shows the Emulators page listing RetroArch, DuckStation, ARMSX2, Dolphin, PPSSPP, Flycast and melonDS with their detected install kind.

Device check `emulators.detected`: Settings -> Emulators lists every emulator installed on the Nova (compared with what the harness finds in `~/Applications` and `flatpak list --system --app`) with its install kind, and no Flathub warning appears (screenshot).

title: The RomM token is stored safely, and the risk is stated
description: Phase 0 logged 'no OS keyring available, credentials are stored in plain text' on armadaOS. Keep RomMix's `credentials.bin` (already written with mode 0600 in `src/main/store.ts`), make its folder 0700, use the OS keyring when one is reachable in both sessions, and never lose the token when switching between Desktop Mode (KWallet may be present) and Game Mode (no keyring). Document the remaining risk in Settings and the README.
acceptance: Unit tests: credentials file 0600, its folder 0700, and both are corrected at start if loosened.

A token written in a session with a keyring is still readable in a session without one: the store either uses one backend consistently (choice recorded in an ADR) or keeps a 0600 fallback copy; a test simulates both orders.
Settings -> Account says where the token is kept ('in a file only your user can read' or 'in the system keyring') and how to revoke it in RomM.

Device check `auth.storage`: in Game Mode (no keyring) the imported token is stored in the test home's credentials file with mode 0600 in a 0700 folder, the backend in use is recorded, and a restart signs in again without pairing.

title: Game manuals open on RomM 5.2.0
description: Phase 0 logged 'refused an image request that is not an asset path {path: roms/3/14/manual/14.pdf}': the asset protocol in `src/main/app.ts` rejects RomM's `path_manual`. Accept manual paths under RomM's resources root (still refusing anything that climbs out of it), so the Manual tab works now and the screensaver collage can use manual pages later (PARITY-33).
acceptance:
`src/main/app.test.ts` gains cases: `roms/

//manual/.pdf` is served; `../` and absolute paths are still refused.
The Docker RomM fixture gets a manual uploaded through `POST /api/roms/{id}/manuals` and `npm run test:romm` opens it through the client.

title: Platform icons never show as broken

Fix the icon-name mapping in `src/config/systems.ts` (PLATFORM_ICON_PATHS tries both the slug and the table's `icon`), remember 404s for the session so they are not asked again, and fall back to a bundled label or glyph in the fork's style (no third-party artwork unless its licence allows MIT redistribution).

`shots:nova` of the Library shows no broken image for GameCube or Wii U.

title: Cheap when idle
description: Phase 0 saw Chromium's GPU process at about 20% CPU in Game Mode. Cut the launcher's background cost so the conservative governor is not kept busy: poll the gamepad with requestAnimationFrame only while the window is visible and input arrived recently (fall back to a slow timer when idle), stop decorative animations and spinners when nothing is loading, honour a reduced-motion setting, and avoid repaint-triggering CSS on idle screens.
acceptance: A test:app scenario measures CPU time of all the app's processes over 60 s idle on Home under Xvfb and fails above a budget recorded in the test (start from the measured baseline, then require at least a 50% cut).
Input latency after idle stays under one frame plus 50 ms (test:app presses a button after 30 s idle and times the focus change).

Device check `idle.cpu`: on the Balanced profile, 60 s idle on Home costs less CPU than the budget in thresholds.json (all Galleon processes, from /proc), and the first internal pad event after the idle period moves focus within one frame plus 50 ms.

title: Select+Start as the exit combo, if the owner wants it
description: The owner originally proposed holding Select+Start about 1 s; Phase 0 showed holding Start already works. Ask in one `needs-human` decision issue whether to keep Start, switch to Select+Start, or allow both.
