The EVIOCGKEY key-state helper described in docs/PLAN.md stays a contingency for the day Chromium stops seeing pads while unfocused.
acceptance: The decision issue is labelled `needs-human`, asks one question, and states the safe default and the date it applies; the answer or the default is quoted in docs/PROGRESS.md and recorded in an ADR.
The hold logic is a pure function with tests (both held 999 ms: nothing; 1,000 ms: fire once; released and held again: fire again), and the setting is in Settings -> Games.
Device check `exit.combo`: synthetic pad events through Galleon's gamepad layer (the code the real pad feeds) for each enabled combo stop the sandboxed RetroArch and Dolphin with their saves intact.

title: The launcher registers itself with Steam
description: Phase 0: Steam's 'Add a Non-Steam Game -> Browse' file picker never opened under KDE on the Nova; a .desktop file had to be written by hand. The fork registers itself: `install.sh` (M0-17) writes the .desktop entry, and `install.sh --add-to-steam` (offered by default, and a button in Settings when Steam is not running) adds a non-Steam shortcut to every `~/.local/share/Steam/userdata/*/config/shortcuts.vdf`: exe = the Steam script, start dir `~/Applications`, launch options `/usr/libexec/armada/armada-game-launch %command%` when that file exists, plus the launcher's artwork in `config/grid/`. It refuses while Steam runs (Steam rewrites the file on exit), offers to close Steam, and backs the file up first. The Decky companion (M3-01) is the route that needs no Desktop Mode at all.
acceptance: A binary-VDF reader and writer with round-trip tests on real-shaped fixtures (types 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x08; other keys preserved).
Steam running is detected (process `steam` or `~/.steam/steam.pid`) and the tool exits with instructions instead of writing.
An existing entry for the same exe is updated, not duplicated.

Device check `steam.shortcut-roundtrip`: a copy of each real shortcuts.vdf (the originals are only read) round-trips byte for byte, and adding then updating a Galleon entry in the copy leaves every other entry unchanged.

title: Sign in by importing stock RomMix's sign-in on first run
description: Phase 0 left stock RomMix v0.20.0 signed in on the Nova. On first run with no server configured, Galleon offers 'Use the RomM sign-in from RomMix': it reads RomMix's settings (`~/.config/rommix/root` pointer or `~/rommix`; `config/settings.json`, whose `server` holds `baseUrl` and `authMode`) and credentials (`config/credentials.bin`: the 4-byte magic `RAW1` then JSON with `clientToken`, or `ENC1` when keyring-encrypted), checks them with GET /api/heartbeat and /api/users/me, and stores them in Galleon's own store, so the owner never pairs again. RomMix's files are only read. Galleon registers as its own RomM device rather than reusing RomMix's device id, so the two apps' save-sync records stay apart. Encrypted or missing credentials fall back to pairing (M1-22).
acceptance: A pure parser reads both RomMix layouts with fixture tests (RAW1 client token, RAW1 OAuth pair, ENC1, a truncated file, a missing pointer), and the importer opens RomMix's files read-only (a test asserts their bytes and mtimes are unchanged).
The offer appears only when no server is configured, and the setup wizard (M4-32) shows it before pairing; declining leads to the normal sign-in.
RomMix's device id is never copied (unit test); in normal use Galleon registers its own device after the import, and in self-test mode it registers nothing.

Device check `import.rommix`: a fresh test home with the import accepted reaches a signed-in Home using the Nova's stock RomMix sign-in, with GET requests only, and stock RomMix's folder is unchanged (manifest).

title: Save-sync spec written from Argosy's code, before any engine change
description: Write `docs/save-sync/SPEC.md` from rommapp/argosy-launcher at 2714d5453b6bbef790987071ab0e82068009532b (read as specification only; GPL-3.0, nothing copied): per system the owner plays (SNES, GBA, PS1, PSP, PS2, GameCube/Wii, Dreamcast), what Argosy uploads on a RomM 5.2.0 server (no SAVE_SYNC in heartbeat, so the legacy handlers in `app/src/main/kotlin/com/nendo/argosy/data/sync/platform/*SaveHandler.kt` and `data/sync/SaveArchiver.kt`, not Sigil): slot, emulator tag, file name, archive shape, how content_hash is computed, when sync runs, how 409 and conflicts are handled (`data/repository/SaveUploader.kt`, `SaveDownloader.kt`, `data/sync/NegotiateInventory.kt`, `SyncCoordinator.kt`, `docs/save-sync-flow.md`, `docs/save-id-to-path.md`). Map each to what RomM 5.2.0 does (`reference/romm-api/openapi-5.2.0.json`).
acceptance: Every statement about Argosy cites file and line at the pinned commit; every statement about RomM cites the 5.2.0 schema or RomM source at tag 5.2.0.
A table per system lists Android emulator/core, Argosy handler, archive shape, emulator tag, and the Linux emulator(s) that could read it, with 'same bytes', 'convertible' or 'not interoperable'.

The spec lists the differences from RomMix's current engine (`src/main/saves.ts`): no negotiate, `overwrite=true` uploads, downloads without device_id/optimistic=false, `.rommix-save.zip` directory archives, shared memory cards skipped.
The evaluator subagent reviews the spec against the cited code and its verdict is in the PR; open questions only a capture can answer are listed for M2-02.

title: Argosy's save shapes confirmed on the owner's server, read-only
description: Instead of a capture run by a person, the device bridge runs `test/device/argosy-shapes.py` (Python 3 standard library) when the nightly request asks for it. With the imported sign-in it finds saves made by Argosy devices (`GET /api/devices`, then `GET /api/saves?rom_id=` for up to 3 games per system, chosen from the server's own lists), downloads each into memory (GET, never with a `device_id`, which would record a sync for a device), and records only its shape: slot, emulator tag, file-name pattern, archive entry names and sizes, whether `content_hash` follows RomM's rule, and updated_at. The bytes are discarded on the device. docs/save-sync/SPEC.md (M2-01) is checked against the report.
acceptance: The script sends only GET requests and never a `device_id` (a unit test checks the file statically: no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, no `device_id`), and a CI test runs it against Docker 5.2.0 seeded as an Argosy device and validates the report layout.
The report holds no save bytes, game titles or account names, and passes the sanitiser with nothing withheld.
Device check `argosy.shapes`: the report from the Nova covers every system the owner has Argosy saves for, and every difference from SPEC.md is resolved in a PR that updates SPEC.md or the fixtures.

title: Golden fixtures and round-trip harness on Docker 5.2.0
description: Build `test/fixtures/saves/<system>/` golden files from SPEC.md (synthetic saves in exactly the shapes Argosy writes, built from the specification, never copied from Argosy's code or from anyone's real saves; cross-checked with the M2-02 shape report once it exists) and add `npm run test:saves`: it seeds Docker 5.2.0 as 'an Argosy device' (a device record with `client: argosy-launcher`, uploads exactly as the spec says), then drives the fork's engine as a second device and asserts the server ends in the expected state; and the reverse.
acceptance: For each system: identical bytes on both sides negotiate to `no_op` twice in a row (Argosy's own proof standard).
Fork upload after an Argosy upload of the same slot is either a conflict or an explicit decision, never a silent overwrite; Argosy's later negotiate sees the fork's upload as `download`.
Fixtures carry no personal data (a test scans them for IPs, tokens and the server host placeholder).
The harness runs in the CI build job on both architectures.
Every fixture names the SPEC.md section it follows.

title: content_hash exactly as RomM computes it
description: Implement `src/main/savehash.ts`: MD5 hex for a plain file; for a zip, MD5 of the sorted `name:md5(entry)` lines joined with newlines, skipping directories (RomM `assets_handler.py`). Use it for every local inventory entry.
acceptance: Unit tests with zips whose entry order differs produce the same hash; directory entries are ignored.
Against Docker 5.2.0, the hash the server stores for each uploaded golden file equals the local hash (test:saves).
Hashing streams files and never loads more than 8 MB into memory at once.

title: Decision engine that agrees with RomM's negotiate
description: Replace RomMix's client-side comparison in `src/main/saves.ts` for the Argosy-compatible path with RomM's own rules (ADR 0002): on 5.2.0, negotiate with the full local inventory and act only on the game in question for a pre-launch check; on 5.3+, scope with `rom_ids`. A per-game shortcut that reads `GET /api/saves?rom_id&device_id` and reproduces `compare_save_state` locally is allowed only if a test proves it decides identically to negotiate for every golden scenario.
acceptance: Capability gating comes from the heartbeat version through `src/main/romm/version.ts` (`atLeast(version, '5.3.0')` for rom_ids), with tests for 5.0, 5.2.0, 5.3.1 and 'development'.
An equivalence test feeds the same scenarios to the engine and to the real negotiate endpoint on Docker 5.2.0 and 5.3.1 and requires identical actions.
A pre-launch check for one game never downloads or uploads another game's save, even though 5.2.0 returns operations for the whole library.
Sessions are completed with operation counts; a session superseded by a newer negotiate is treated as finished, not as an error.

title: Transfers the way Argosy makes them
description: Uploads send `rom_id`, `emulator`, `slot=autosave`, `device_id`, `session_id` and `overwrite=false` (`src/main/romm/client.ts` `uploadSave` currently sends `overwrite=true`); a 409 becomes a conflict for the user. Downloads use `device_id`, `optimistic=false`, write to a temporary file, fsync, rename, then `POST /api/saves/{id}/downloaded`.
acceptance: `overwrite=true` is sent only from the explicit 'Keep this device's save' choice (test asserts every other call site sends false).
A failed or interrupted write never calls `/downloaded` (fault-injection test), so the server never records this device as current.
Retrying an upload with identical content is idempotent on 5.2.0 and 5.3.1 (no duplicate slot rows; test:saves).
Play sessions recorded during the session are sent with the session's completion (`play_sessions`).

title: One safe writer for every save on disk
description: Route every write into an emulator's save tree through one function that refuses to replace a directory with a file (the Argosy fork's Dolphin memory-card bug), backs up the file it replaces (RomMix `keepBackup`), writes atomically and fsyncs. Add regression tests for the Argosy fork's bug list (docs/research/argosy_fork_inventory.md, Q7).
acceptance: `grep` in CI finds no `writeFile`/`rename`/`rm` into save directories outside the writer module (allow-list test).
Tests: a directory at the destination is refused and logged; a normal overwrite and a create still work; two concurrent writers to one save are serialised.
Backups are kept per game, the last 5 by default, under `~/<name>/saves/`.

title: Per system, how saves travel (owner decision with a safe default)
description: Open a `needs-human` decision issue with a plain-language table per system: (A) run the same libretro core as Argosy in RetroArch, saves move unchanged; or (B) run the standalone emulator (DuckStation, PPSSPP, Dolphin, Flycast, ARMSX2), with an adapter where the spec says one is possible. Safe default after 72 hours without an answer, recorded in an ADR: (A) for every system where SPEC.md says Argosy's core runs on Linux aarch64 with 'same bytes'; otherwise (B) where the spec says 'convertible'; otherwise 'not interoperable, saves stay on each side', said plainly in the app. Record the outcome in `docs/save-sync/SYSTEM-CHOICES.md` and set the default emulator per system from it.
acceptance: The issue explains each choice's trade-off in one or two sentences a non-developer can follow, citing the spec's 'same bytes / convertible / not interoperable' column, and states the safe default and its date.
SYSTEM-CHOICES.md records per system the owner's answer, or the default and the date it applied, and the defaults in settings follow it.
The choice can be changed per system in Settings, and the final acceptance session (M8-07) re-confirms it.

title: SNES and GBA saves round-trip with Argosy
description: RetroArch .srm on both sides. Use the emulator tag and file naming Argosy uses for these cores (from the spec), read RetroArch's real save folder from its config, and sync under the `autosave` slot.
acceptance: test:saves passes for the SNES and GBA golden files in both directions.

Device check `saves.snes-gba`: the SNES and GBA payloads write `.srm` files in RetroArch's sandbox; Galleon finds them where RetroArch's config says, archives them as SPEC.md says Argosy does, uploads them to the on-device fake RomM (M2-20, never the owner's server), downloads them byte-identical into an empty sandbox, and the owner's real RetroArch save folder is unchanged.
The real Android-to-Linux round trip for this system is part of Gate 2 in the final acceptance session (M2-19).

title: PlayStation saves round-trip
description: Per the choice in SYSTEM-CHOICES.md (M2-08): RetroArch with the Android core (same .srm), or DuckStation with a converter between DuckStation's per-game memory card and the Android core's save (both raw 128 KiB card images where the spec confirms it).
acceptance: The converter, if used, is a pure function with golden tests both ways and refuses inputs that are not 131,072-byte card images.
test:saves passes for the PS1 golden files.

Device check `saves.ps1`: a memory card in the spec's shape seeded in DuckStation's sandbox (or the Android core's save, per SYSTEM-CHOICES.md) is converted, uploaded to the on-device fake RomM and restored byte-identical; both discs of a multi-disc game share it.
The real Android-to-Linux round trip for this system is part of Gate 2 in the final acceptance session (M2-19).

title: PSP saves round-trip
description: PPSSPP's SAVEDATA folders, archived in the exact shape Argosy's PSP handler uses (prefix bundle by game id, per the spec), never RomMix's `.rommix-save.zip`.
acceptance: The archive builder produces byte-identical zip entry names and layout to the golden Argosy archive and the same content_hash for the same files.
Device check `saves.psp`: a SAVEDATA folder seeded in PPSSPP's sandbox is archived with the golden entry names and content_hash, uploaded to the on-device fake RomM and restored identically.
The real Android-to-Linux round trip for this system is part of Gate 2 in the final acceptance session (M2-19).

title: PS2 folder memory cards round-trip
description: ARMSX2 on both sides, folder memory cards only (Argosy syncs nothing else for PS2). Detect whether ARMSX2's slot 1 card is a folder card; if not, explain how to switch and offer to convert nothing automatically. Follow a custom data folder if ARMSX2 is configured with one.
acceptance: Reading `~/.config/ARMSX2/inis/PCSX2.ini` decides folder vs file card; tests for both and for a custom memcard folder.
The archive shape matches Argosy's PS2 folder handler for a single game's save directory inside the folder card.

Device check `saves.ps2`: the Nova's real `PCSX2.ini` is read (never changed) to decide folder or file cards, and a folder card seeded in ARMSX2's sandbox round-trips through the on-device fake RomM in Argosy's shape.
The real Android-to-Linux round trip for this system is part of Gate 2 in the final acceptance session (M2-19).

title: GameCube and Wii saves round-trip
description: Dolphin standalone on Linux against Argosy's GCI handler (GameCube) and Wii title saves, per the spec; require Dolphin's GCI-folder mode for GameCube if that is what makes per-game saves possible, and say so.
acceptance: Golden tests convert between Argosy's archive and Dolphin's GCI folder layout without touching other games' GCI files.
The writer never deletes or replaces the memory-card directory itself (regression test for the fork's 2026-09-19 bug).

Device check `saves.gc-wii`: GCI files and a Wii title save seeded in Dolphin's sandbox user folder round-trip through the on-device fake RomM without touching the other games' GCI files or the memory-card folder itself.
The real Android-to-Linux round trip for this system is part of Gate 2 in the final acceptance session (M2-19).

title: Dreamcast saves round-trip
description: Flycast standalone against Argosy's Dreamcast handler (built-in flycast core VMU), per the spec; use per-game VMUs if Flycast can, otherwise declare it shared with a clear reason.
acceptance: Golden tests for the VMU mapping both ways, or a documented 'not interoperable' decision recorded in SYSTEM-CHOICES.md (M2-08).

Device check `saves.dc`: a VMU seeded in Flycast's sandbox round-trips through the on-device fake RomM, or the app shows the 'Dreamcast saves do not travel' notice (screenshot) when SYSTEM-CHOICES.md says so.
The real Android-to-Linux round trip for this system is part of Gate 2 in the final acceptance session (M2-19).

title: Save states only where they can load
description: States are plain per-ROM uploads with no slot, device or conflict logic, and only load in the same core. Sync states only where both sides run the same core and version family; elsewhere keep them local and say so on the Saves tab.
acceptance: A rule table (system, emulator) -> 'states sync' is data with tests; RomMix's `STATE_PULL_LIMIT` behaviour is kept for syncing systems.
The Saves tab labels local-only states clearly (screenshot).

title: Conflicts are decided by the player, explicitly
description: Adapt `src/renderer/src/screens/Game/SaveTransfer.tsx` and the Saves tab to show a conflict as two columns (this device / RomM, with device names from `origin_device_id`, times and sizes) and three explicit choices: keep this device's (upload with overwrite), keep RomM's (download and confirm), or skip. Pressing a cover or moving focus never resolves anything.
acceptance: test:app drives a conflict created on Docker-free fake RomM (`test/app/server.ts` gains 409 and device_syncs support) and checks each choice's resulting calls.
Focus stays on the same choice when the list changes (the Argosy fork's dangerous-neighbour rule).
`shots:nova` includes the conflict dialog at 1280x960.

title: Sync around every session, durable across sleep and reboots
description: Pre-launch check with a cancellable overlay (checking save -> downloading -> launching), upload after the emulator exits, a persistent queue of pending uploads that survives suspend, crashes and offline time, and a visible 'All saves uploaded' state so the owner knows it is safe to reboot into Android.
acceptance: The pending-upload queue is a journal on disk; killing the app mid-upload and restarting resumes it (test).
The Home screen and the Decky panel (M3) show 'All saves uploaded' only when the queue is empty and the last negotiate said no_op for every game played since boot.
The overlay's Cancel stops the launch, finishes any write in progress, and leaves nothing half-written.

Device check `saves.journal`: against the on-device fake RomM, playing the RetroArch payload, quitting, then killing Galleon mid-upload and restarting it finishes the upload from the journal; 'All saves uploaded' appears within a minute with the fake server up, says saves are waiting while it is stopped, and clears when it is back (screenshots).

title: Play time reported to RomM
description: Record session start and end around each launch (emulators and Steam games), send them with the sync session's completion or through `POST /api/play-sessions` (batches up to 100), and show PLAYED as RomM's total across devices (RomMix's `playTime`).
acceptance: Sessions shorter than 5 s are dropped; offline sessions are queued and sent later (tests).
test:romm asserts the sessions appear in `GET /api/play-sessions?rom_id=` on 5.2.0.

title: Gate 2: saves travel between Android and Linux (in the final acceptance session)
description: The real Android-to-Linux-to-Android round trip needs the owner's hands (Argosy runs on Android) and the owner's real saves, so it is the Gate 2 part of the final acceptance session (M8-07), done once, after every per-system device check passes. Before it, the local Claude session keeps a read-only copy of the server's saves for the games used (GET only), so nothing can be lost.
acceptance: Every per-system feature M2-09..M2-14 passes its device check before Gate 2 is scheduled.

Acceptance session: for each system you play (the script lists them), save in Argosy on Android, continue that save in Galleon on Linux, save again, and continue in Argosy. Neither side asks you to choose between two saves, and RomM's web page shows one current save per game. Systems marked 'do not travel' in SYSTEM-CHOICES.md show that notice instead.
The results are in `acceptance/<date>/results.json` and PLAN.md links them; a failure reopens that system's feature and never changes the stack.

title: Save checks on the device without the real server
description: Ship a minimal fake RomM in the device bundle (`test/device/fake-romm/`, built from `test/app/server.ts` plus the save, device and negotiate endpoints the M2 engine uses, in RomM 5.2.0's shapes from `reference/romm-api/openapi-5.2.0.json`) and run it on 127.0.0.1 with the Electron binary inside the AppImage in Node mode (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, after `--appimage-extract` into the test folder), so Galleon's real save engine can upload and download on the Nova while the owner's server is only ever read.
acceptance: The fake server listens only on 127.0.0.1 on a random port, and run.sh stops it on exit and in `--cleanup` (it also runs inside the bridge's systemd unit, which ends it).
Its save endpoints pass the same contract tests as Docker 5.2.0 for the calls the engine makes (one shared test runs against both in CI).
Device check `saves.fake-server`: the fake server starts on the Nova, and the self-test pointed at it uploads and downloads one save while `safety.server-readonly` still passes for the real server.

title: Decky companion: QAM status and a quit button
description: A small non-root Decky plugin in `decky/` (TypeScript frontend, no Python backend unless needed) that reads the core socket: Quick Access panel with current game, download progress, 'All saves uploaded', and a 'Quit game' button; plus 'Add/repair shortcut' using `SteamClient.Apps.AddShortcut` with a gamepad controller template. CI builds the zip as a release asset. The launcher keeps working when Decky is broken.
acceptance: The plugin builds in CI with pinned @decky packages, and its licence and the @decky packages' licences are recorded in DEPENDENCIES.md.
With no launcher running the panel says so; with the socket unreachable it never throws.

The panel can install or update the launcher AppImage into `~/Applications` and add its shortcut with `SteamClient.Apps.AddShortcut` (Armada Store's method), so a fresh setup needs no Desktop Mode once Decky has the plugin (installed from its release URL with Decky's developer option).

Acceptance session: install the plugin zip in Decky (the script gives the exact steps), open Quick Access during a game, see the game and save status, and use 'Quit game' to return to Galleon with the save intact.

title: Start in the launcher when the Nova boots (opt-in)
description: Settings -> System -> Start on boot, available only when the launcher was started from Steam (it knows its `SteamGameId`): writes `~/.config/gamescope-session-plus/sessions.d/steam` containing one marked line `CLIENTCMD+=" steam://rungameid/<gameid>"`, preserving anything else in the file; turning it off removes only that line.
acceptance: Unit tests: create, preserve foreign lines, remove only the marked line, refuse when SteamGameId is unknown.
Never touches `/etc` or `/usr`, and never sets CLIENTCMD in `~/.config/environment.d/`.
Settings shows the recovery path: hold Select during the boot splash for Desktop Mode (Armada's own escape).

Acceptance session: turn Start on boot on, reboot, and Galleon opens by itself after Steam starts; turn it off, reboot, and Steam opens as before. (Attended on purpose: an unattended reboot that goes wrong could leave the Nova in a boot loop.)

title: Sleep in the background while something else has the screen
description: When a Steam game or an emulator has focus, stop rendering and polling (renderer suspended, intervals paused), resume when focus returns. Detect focus from window blur/visibility and, where `xprop` is available, gamescope's `GAMESCOPE_FOCUSED_APP` against the launcher's own `SteamAppId`.
acceptance: A focus-state module with tests for both signals and for a missing `xprop`.
test:app confirms timers and frame callbacks stop while suspended and restart on focus.

Device check `focus.suspend`: while the sandboxed emulator, then the test target shortcut, has the screen, Galleon's renderer runs no frame callbacks or timers, and it redraws within 5 s of getting focus back with no black frame (screenshot).

title: Downloads survive sleep and Wi-Fi drops
description: Downloads resume after s2idle or fake suspend: keep `.part` files with ETag/Last-Modified, resume with `Range` and `If-Range`, take a logind delay inhibitor (never block) through `systemd-inhibit` or `busctl` on PrepareForSleep to checkpoint, and after wake wait for NetworkManager connectivity FULL before retrying with back-off.
acceptance: `src/main/romm/transfer.ts` sends If-Range on resume and restarts from zero when the server answers 200 instead of 206 (test with the fake server).
A wake detector (monotonic vs wall-clock gap, plus PrepareForSleep where available) triggers the connectivity wait (unit tests with fakes).
No retry storm: back-off is capped and logged.

Device check `network.resume`: during a capped download the self-test's transfer fault injection drops the connection twice and simulates a wake (a clock jump); the download resumes with Range and If-Range from where it was, and the capped back-off is logged without a retry storm.
Acceptance session (informational): put the Nova to sleep with the power button for a minute during a download; it continues after waking.

title: Exit and power actions that fit Game Mode
description: Under Steam Game Mode, the quit dialog's Sleep/Restart/Turn off (RomMix's `src/main/power.ts`) defer to Steam: offer 'Back to Steam' and 'Switch to Desktop' (Armada's `steamos-session-select desktop`), and keep the systemctl actions only outside Game Mode.
acceptance: Mode detection (gamescope session, SteamGameId) is a pure function with tests; the dialog shows the right set in each mode (test:app with environment overrides).
Device check `gamemode.detect`: in Game Mode the quit dialog offers Back to Steam and Switch to Desktop, and no systemctl power actions (screenshot; nothing is executed).

title: On-screen keyboard that works with the pad
description: An in-app keyboard for every text field (server address, search, collection names), because Steam's keyboard does not reliably appear for non-Steam apps. Layouts for URL, text and numbers; the pad types, B deletes, Start confirms.
acceptance: Every text input opens the in-app keyboard when focused with the pad (test:app walks the sign-in and search screens with the pad only).
`shots:nova` includes the keyboard over the sign-in screen.
Device check `keyboard.osk`: the internal pad driver types a search and a server address with the in-app keyboard (screenshots).

title: In-game menu without stealing the screen
description: Bring the Argosy fork's in-game bar (title, emulator/core, PLAYED, SESSION, achievements; actions) to Linux without mapping a window over the game: in the Decky panel, and for RetroArch through its network command interface (`network_cmd_enable` in the appended config) for save state, load state, reset, disc swap and quit. Standalone emulators keep their own menus.
acceptance: RetroArch commands are sent over UDP to localhost only, with tests against a fake listener.
Reset sits apart from Quit and asks to confirm (dangerous-neighbour rule).
Device check `retroarch.netcmd`: with the sandboxed RetroArch running the SNES payload, Galleon's UDP commands save a state, load it and quit, and RetroArch's log confirms each.
Acceptance session (informational): the same from the Quick Access panel (M3-01).

title: Controller check and Steam Input guidance
description: The pre-flight lists every controller the app can see (the post-v0.20.0 upstream commits 68697e0 and 990e55e3 do this; port them once their test:app failure is fixed) and explains which Steam Input template to choose for the launcher's shortcut, since every emulator inherits it.
acceptance: The upstream commits are ported with their tests, and test:app passes on both architectures.
The guidance text is in all four catalogues and names the template Armada's store uses for its apps.
Device check `controllers.listed`: the pre-flight lists the Nova's controller as Galleon sees it in Game Mode (screenshot).
Acceptance session (informational): with the template the guidance names, the buttons work in every emulator (M7-12).

title: Updates arrive on the Nova without a computer
description: End to end on the device: the in-app updater (Automatic by default) takes the Nova from one nightly to the next, verifying the checksum; `install.sh` works again as a repair path.
acceptance: The updater's Steam-launch limitation (cannot restart itself) is explained on screen with 'quit and press Play again'.
Device check `update.verify` (shared with M0-13) passes, and after a staged update in the test home the screen explains 'quit and press Play again' (screenshot).

title: Local library index for discovery features
description: RomMix deliberately keeps no local copy of the library (TODO.md, 'A copy of the whole library on this disk'), but Series, genre counts, random pick and offline browsing need one. Write an ADR, then build a lean index (id, platform, names, sizes, files summary, genres, franchises, collections, companies, release year, HLTB, missing_from_fs, updated_at) kept current with `updated_after`, deletions from `GET /api/roms/identifiers`, `with_char_index/with_filter_values/with_rom_id_index=false`, a weekly full pass, and startup jobs owned by a service rather than by any screen.
acceptance: The ADR records why RomMix's earlier decision no longer holds for this fork and what stays live (search, per-user fields).
An incremental pass with nothing changed costs one `updated_after` page plus one identifiers call (test against Docker 5.2.0 counting requests).
The first full build for a 4,206-row library fits in under 60 MB on disk (measured with the synthetic library scaled up in a test).
Startup connect, the weekly sync and the favourites refresh run from a main-process service and still run when Home is replaced (test).

title: Design system: the Nova theme
description: Implement the Argosy fork's visual language as a theme and layout set (docs/research/argosy-fork-design-spec.md): black or charcoal ground, white and four greys, hairlines #1c1c1c, one swappable accent (amber default plus mint, sky, rose, lime, slate) reserved for selection and things in motion, IBM Plex Mono (SIL OFL, shipped with its licence in `src/renderer/src/assets/fonts/`), weights one step heavier, type at 1.2x of the 1024x768 canvas scaled to 1280x960, TEXT SIZE 100-130%, square corners, no painted system chrome.
acceptance: Tokens live in one stylesheet under `src/renderer/src/styles/themes/` plus CSS variables; no screen hard-codes a colour (lint rule or test greps `#[0-9a-f]{3,6}` outside theme files).
A contrast test checks every grey on both grounds against the type sizes it is used at.
`shots:nova` contact sheet reviewed: the accent appears only on the focused item and on moving progress.

title: One selection look and calm motion
description: The focused item's label turns accent only where A acts, with one 2 px accent mark (left bar on rows, underline on inline items, inner ring on tiles) and a 15% band on full-width rows; colour-only transitions of about 120 ms; animate colour, opacity and width only, never size or position (docs/research/argosy-fork-design-spec.md, 'One selection look', 'Motion').
acceptance: A shared focus component in `src/renderer/src/components/` is used by every focusable element; a test:app scan finds no focused element without the mark.
A CSS lint test fails on transitions or animations of width/height/top/left/transform on grid tiles.
No row ever shows two accent spots, and items where A does nothing step one grey brighter instead (screenshots).

title: Grids that stay smooth at 1,300 games
description: Replace the grow-forever paging grid (`src/renderer/src/paging.ts`, PAGE_SIZE 60 appended to the DOM) with windowed rendering: only rows near the viewport exist, focus movement never reflows, images decode off the main thread at tile size, and covers are cached on disk at display size.
acceptance: With a 1,300-game fake platform, DOM node count stays under 600 at any scroll position (test:app).
The frame-time overlay's scripted 30 s scroll under Xvfb shows no regression against the M1 baseline recorded in PROGRESS.md.

Device check `grid.scroll@performance`: scrolling a 1,000+ game platform top to bottom and back shows p95 frame time at or under 16.7 ms and dropped frames at or under 3% on the Performance profile, with no regression against the M1 baseline recorded in PROGRESS.md.

title: File-state dot everywhere
description: One dot at the bottom-left of every cover and row: hollow grey ring = on the server, solid grey = queued, solid accent plus a 2 px accent hairline filling left to right = downloading (the line appears only once bytes move), solid white = on this device; multi-disc games aggregate their discs.
acceptance: The state is computed by one pure function from the download queue and the install index, including multi-disc aggregation (unit tests for all four states and partial discs).
`shots:nova` includes a grid with all four states (fake server can hold a download at 40%).

title: Now playing home
description: Home becomes Now playing (docs/research/argosy-fork-design-spec.md): left a two-column feed of up to 12 recently played games, right the selected game's preview in a 4:3 frame over title, year, DEVELOPER / PUBLISHER / GENRE / FILE (disc count and size), a hairline and the status row with transfer progress; A play or download, X details, Y preview audio, RB Browse, B back; empty state points at Browse.
acceptance: Recently played comes from RomM's `last_played` plus local sessions, most recent first (test).
Controls behave as listed (test:app with the pad).
`shots:nova` shows the populated and empty states.

title: Preview video with sound
description: Play RomM's per-game preview (`path_video`, served from the resources mount) through a protocol handler that supports Range, start it about 250 ms after selection settles, cut (never fade) on change, loop, sound on, black when there is none, a 750 MB LRU disk cache, and stop it under the screensaver, while a game runs and when the window is hidden.
acceptance: The protocol handler answers Range requests with 206 and validates paths like the image protocol (unit tests).
The debounce and cache eviction are pure modules with tests; a d-pad sweep across 20 tiles opens at most one stream.

Device check `video.preview`: a sweep across 20 tiles opens at most one stream, the settled selection's video starts within 500 ms (a bundled public-domain clip when the library has no preview videos), and grid p95 during playback stays within the M4-04 threshold.

title: Preview audio toggle
description: Y toggles preview audio globally, shown as PREVIEW AUDIO / MUTED on the video badge and in the header; Browse honours it; the setting persists.
acceptance: Persisted in settings and covered by a test; the badge appears in `shots:nova`.

title: Browse: grid and metadata bar
description: Per-platform 5-column grid of 4:3 tiles with LB/RB to change platform and header counts; a metadata bar along the bottom (156 px at 1.2x type, scaled for 1280x960) whose right half is the selected game's video under the left-to-right scrim; three metadata rows (DEVELOPER / PUBLISHER / GENRE, then PLAYED / TO BEAT / ACHIEVEMENTS, plus TRANSFER while downloading) with a 90 ms crossfade on selection change (docs/research/argosy-fork-design-spec.md).
acceptance: LB/RB cycle platforms in RomM order and wrap (test:app).
TO BEAT comes from RomM's HLTB data where present and is omitted otherwise.
`shots:nova` shows Browse with and without a download in progress.

title: The bar rises into a panel
description: A raises the bar into a 416 px panel (scaled): the video grows to a 512x384 letterboxed frame, the plain cover in a white hairline, the description and hints A PLAY/DOWNLOAD, X DETAILS, B CLOSE fade in; the grid dims but never moves; B drops it back.
acceptance: The grid's tile positions are identical before, during and after the panel (test:app compares bounding boxes).
Panel and bar are one element at two heights (no remount; video keeps playing).

title: Title-aware cover crop and selection reveal
description: Match RomM's per-game `logo.png` against the cover once per game in a worker (blurred-edge plus luma cross-correlation over scales, accept only confident matches), store one 0..1 offset per game, and crop 4:3 tiles to keep the title, centred when unsure. The selected tile zooms out to the whole cover over a blurred, dimmed copy without changing size.
acceptance: The matcher is a pure function tested on fixture covers with known logo positions (including 'no logo' and 'not confident' cases returning centre).
Analysis is batched, time-limited, retried at most three times and never re-run on download ticks.
`shots:nova` shows a cover cropped to its title and a selected tile revealing the whole cover.

title: Cover flight into details
description: Opening details from the Browse panel fades the rest of Browse to black while the cover glides to the detail screen's cover frame (376x282 canvas px, scaled), then the route changes; input is ignored mid-flight.
acceptance: The flight uses transform/opacity on a detached copy only (not on grid tiles) and lasts about 320 ms.
Pressed buttons during the flight are dropped (test:app).

title: Game details in the fork layout
description: Left: the plain cover in a white hairline, status, and an action rail (play/download, delete, favourite, hide, versions, discs, emulator and core, saves, collections). Right: metadata, description, screenshots (focus follows the d-pad), achievements, and MORE IN <series>. RomMix's tabs (Details, Saves, Files, Screenshots, Manual, Achievements, Versions) are restyled, not dropped.
acceptance: Every action of the inherited game page is still reachable with the pad (test:app visits each `data-action`).
The screenshot strip's focus ring follows d-pad moves (test).
`shots:nova` covers each part of the page.

title: Genre filter and ALL / ON DEVICE
description: A 34 px genre strip under the Browse header: LT/RT step through genres ordered by count, SELECT flips ALL / ON DEVICE; applies to Browse and Series, never to Now playing; remembered between launches; no accent in the strip.
acceptance: Genre counts come from the local index and match RomM for the fixture library (test).
Both choices persist across restarts (test).

title: Series / IP screen
description: IPs are IGDB franchises spanning two or more systems, plus multi-system collections with no franchise; each opens to its series grouped by platform; details get MORE IN <series> (up to 7 games) ending in ALL OF <IP>. Names containing commas must not split.
acceptance: Grouping is a pure function over the local index with tests, including comma-containing franchise names and games in several collections.
The screen fills in under one second for the scaled synthetic library (test).

title: Collections as a mosaic
description: One RomM collection at a time as a mosaic that scrolls down; LB/RB step around the ring (genres first, then game modes, each largest first, then the user's and smart collections); A opens the focused game.
acceptance: Collections come from `/api/collections`, `/api/collections/smart` and `/api/collections/virtual` (fake server supports all three).
`shots:nova` shows the mosaic.

title: Drawer on Start
description: Start opens a drawer: Now playing, Browse, Series, Collections, Downloads, Saves, Apps, Settings, with counts only when something needs attention (failed downloads, save conflicts) and an account row.
acceptance: Counts update live from the queue and the save engine (test:app).
`shots:nova` shows the drawer with one count.

title: L3 quick menu
description: L3 opens search (fuzzy), random pick, most played, top unplayed, recent and favourites; each game row shows 64x48 art and the file-state dot, and updates live when a download finishes.
acceptance: Fuzzy search is a pure function with tests (typos, articles, roman numerals).
A download finishing while the menu is open turns the dot white without reopening (test:app).

title: R3 quick settings
description: R3 opens quick settings: accent, ground, text size, preview audio, navigation sounds, the frame-time overlay, and Armada's performance profile where it can be read and set without root (otherwise a hint to use Armada Control).
acceptance: Each control changes the setting in place with left/right (test:app).
The performance-profile control is hidden when the system offers no unprivileged way to change it (detection unit-tested).

title: Settings hub
description: Fork knobs first (ACCENT, GROUND, TEXT SIZE, SCREENSAVER AFTER, SCREENSAVER FIELD, PREVIEW AUDIO), changed in place with left/right; then server, sync, RetroAchievements, storage, emulators, BIOS, Steam, graphics, updates, about. Remembers focus and scroll.
acceptance: Every inherited setting from `src/renderer/src/screens/Settings/tabs/` is still reachable (test:app).
Focus and scroll are restored when returning to the hub (test).

title: Notices that never steal focus
description: Square cards with a 2 px left mark (white info, grey warning, red error); only a running task's hairline uses the accent; a persistent running-task card; drawn inside the main window and queued while a game runs.
acceptance: `src/renderer/src/Toasts.tsx` restyled; test:app confirms no extra window and queued delivery after a game.

title: Screensaver
description: After 2.5 idle minutes (off, 1, 2, 2.5, 3, 5, 10): black with a soft accent noise field rendered at about 10 fps, clock top left, a random installed or library game bottom left (cover, platform and year, title, time to beat, A OPEN), and a 4:3 collage of that game's screenshots plus one page of its manual; a new game every 30 s; any button wakes, A opens details; video and audio stop.
acceptance: The collage layout is a pure function choosing one of three grid patterns, each picture used once, empty slots as hairline frames (tests).
Manual pages come through the M1-25 path, are cached (100 MB cap, 40 MB per file) and rendered at 900 px.
The noise field costs under 2 ms per frame on the Xvfb runner and runs only while the saver shows.

title: Achievements from RomM
description: Per-game achievements and progress from RomM's RetroAchievements data on details, the Browse bar and the in-game panel; the fetch retries after errors, caches per user, and refreshes after a session.
acceptance: A failed fetch is retried with back-off within the session, not only after restart (test).
Cache keys include the RomM user id (test).

title: Downloads screen in the fork layout
description: ACTIVE / QUEUED / FINISHED rows with small cover, platform and status, the accent hairline, and the M1-18 line '15% - 613.6 MB / 3.8 GB - 41.4 MB/s - 1m 20s left'; storage wait reads 'NEED 4.2 GB, AVAILABLE 1.1 GB'; failures show the reason and Retry; X cancels; the 'on this device' list with sizes and free space stays.
acceptance: Focus survives rows moving between sections (test:app).

Device check `download.queue`: three small ROMs queued in the test home run one after another, X on the internal pad driver cancels one, the rows keep their places and focus never jumps (screenshots), and every file is deleted afterwards.

title: Saves screen in the fork layout
description: Header with device name, saves from this device, connection; NEEDS A DECISION (M2-16 choices); IN PROGRESS; SAVED GAMES with readable status (SERVER NEWER, PENDING UPLOAD, UP TO DATE, NOT SYNCED: reason); Y runs a check; unreadable save folders are named.
acceptance: Statuses map one-to-one from the engine's states with no state shown as uploading before bytes move (test).
`shots:nova` shows each section.

title: Apps screen
description: Other apps in 4:3 hairline frames: Steam's non-Steam shortcuts (from M5-05) and Armada Store apps (`~/.local/share/applications/armada-*.desktop`), with hide and reorder; launching goes through Steam for shortcuts so Steam tracks them.
acceptance: Order and hidden state persist (test).
`shots:nova` shows the screen in reorder mode.

title: Every control on the pad, and a footer that says what buttons do
description: D-pad, face buttons, shoulders, triggers, Start, Select, L3, R3 all have a job on the screens where they help; a contextual footer shows the current bindings and hides when there is nothing useful to say; touch still works where it existed; no painted status bar, clock (outside the screensaver) or battery.
acceptance: A binding table per screen is data; test:app checks the footer matches it.
Every screen is fully operable without touch or keyboard (test:app pad-only walk).

title: Every inherited surface in the new look
description: Restyle what remains from RomMix (setup and emulator wizards, dialogs, BIOS, Emulators, pre-flight, update panel, collections dialog) so nothing leaks the old themes, including the light themes; the fork theme is the default and RomMix's themes stay selectable only if they still render correctly.
acceptance: A test renders every screen in the fork theme and fails on computed colours outside the token set (test:app).
`shots:nova` contact sheet reviewed screen by screen in the PR.

title: Library hygiene: folding and filters
description: Fold RomM sibling rows with the same display name into one game with a version picker at download time (never at launch), join per-disc rows into one multi-disc game, and add sync filters: hide prototypes, betas, demos, unlicensed, hacks, chosen regions and hidden games.
acceptance: Folding is a pure function over index rows with tests from the fixture library's shapes.
Filters persist and apply to Browse, Series, search and counts consistently (tests).

title: Favourites, hide and ratings stay in RomM
description: Favourite, hide and rate from details and the quick menu; changes go to RomM (`PUT /api/roms/{id}/props` and the favourites collection) and queue while offline.
acceptance: test:romm asserts each change round-trips on 5.2.0; offline changes are sent on reconnect (test).

title: Emulator and core per platform and per game; disc and memory-card pickers
description: Per-platform choice exists in RomMix (Emulators -> Platforms, 'Run with...'); add per-game overrides of emulator and core shown with the inherited default, a disc picker for multi-disc games, and a memory-card picker where an emulator has several cards.
acceptance: Overrides persist per ROM id and change the save location consistently (tests on `saves()` context).
`shots:nova` shows the per-game override and the disc picker.

title: First-run wizard and pairing in the new look
description: Restyle `src/renderer/src/screens/Wizards/Setup/` at 4:3 with the M1-21 address probing and M1-22 pairing screen, ending with the SD-card choice (M1-10) and the emulator check (M1-23).
acceptance: test:app completes the wizard with the pad only against the fake server.
`shots:nova` shows each wizard page.

title: UI acceptance on the Nova
description: The owner judges the redesigned launcher on the device: legibility at arm's length and feel. The measured part is already settled by the device checks of M4-04 and M4-34, which must pass first.
acceptance: The newest device results pass `grid.scroll@performance` (M4-04) and `grid.scroll@balanced` (M4-34) before the session is scheduled.

Acceptance session: walk Now playing, Browse (with the panel), details, Series, Collections, Downloads, Saves and Settings for ten minutes. Text is readable at arm's length, it feels at least as smooth as Steam's library, and you would rather use it than Steam's library.

title: Smooth on Armada's Balanced profile too
description: Phase 0 passed smoothness only on the Performance profile. Make the redesigned UI light enough that browsing is smooth on Balanced (conservative governor, capped clocks), so the launcher does not need Performance just to scroll: cheap focus moves, no layout work per d-pad press, decoded covers at tile size, video decode only for the settled selection, and a 'light browse' setting that turns off preview video and the reveal zoom if needed.
acceptance: test:app runs the scripted Browse scroll with CPU throttled (Chromium CPU throttling rate 4 through the DevTools protocol) and records frame-time p90 and janky share; the PR shows before/after.
The light-browse setting exists in R3 quick settings and is remembered.
Device check `grid.scroll@balanced`: on the Balanced profile the same scroll shows p95 frame time at or under 16.7 ms and dropped frames at or under 5%.

title: Steam games as a first-class platform
description: Installed Steam games appear in Now playing, Browse (a Steam platform), search and the quick menu, with art from the user's custom grid images, Steam's `appcache/librarycache` (flat files and per-appid folders) and finally Steam's CDN; playtime and last played from `localconfig.vdf` where present.
acceptance: Art lookup order is a pure function with tests for both librarycache layouts.
Steam games never enter RomM sync, save sync or downloads (tests).
Device check `steam.list` also shows installed Steam games as a Steam platform with art found for each (counts only), offered to start but not started.

title: Coming back from a Steam game
description: After a Steam game exits, the launcher returns to the front and redraws; while it runs, the launcher is suspended (M3-03).
acceptance: Device check `steam.return`: three times in a row, after the 'Galleon Device Test Target' shortcut started from Galleon exits, Galleon is in front within 5 s and redrawn, never a black screen (screenshots).

title: Living with 'Launch Multiple Games'
description: Steam may show a 'Launch Multiple Games' prompt because the launcher is itself a running shortcut, and 'Close previous game' would kill it. Detect the outcome (the launcher killed vs still running), and apply the mitigation the `steam.launch` results support: guidance on screen before the first Steam launch, and relaunch through the Decky companion or Start on boot if the launcher was closed.
acceptance: The chosen mitigation is recorded in an ADR citing the `steam.launch` results.
Device check `steam.launch` (M1-14): after the mitigation lands, the target starts and Galleon survives in three consecutive nightly runs.

title: Install Steam games you own but have not installed
description: For owned apps that Steam lists locally but are not installed, offer Install, handing off to Steam with `steam://install/<appid>` and showing Steam's progress state from the appmanifest when it appears.
acceptance: Owned-but-not-installed detection is a pure function over Steam's local files with fixture tests; nothing is downloaded by the launcher itself.
Acceptance session: pick a game you own but have not installed and press Install in Galleon; Steam starts installing it, and Galleon shows it as installing, then installed.

title: Read non-Steam shortcuts
description: Parse binary `shortcuts.vdf` (read-only here; writing is M1-29) to list non-Steam shortcuts with appid, name, exe and launch options, and compute their 64-bit gameid `(appid << 32) | 0x02000000` for launching through `steam://rungameid/`.
acceptance: Reader tests on fixtures, including signed int32 appids and unknown keys.
The launcher hides its own shortcut from the list.

title: Favourite means ready to play
description: Marking a game as a favourite queues its download in the background (behind anything the user started), respects free space and the SD-card choice, and offers to remove the download when it is unfavourited (never automatically).
acceptance: The queue policy is a pure function with tests (priority, space check, unfavourite while queued cancels, unfavourite when installed asks).
Favourites set from another device (RomM) are picked up at the next sync and queued too (test with Docker RomM).

Device check `favourite.predownload`: a favourite set in the test home (the server's favourites are only read) queues the smallest SNES title in the background behind a user-started download; it completes, and unfavouriting asks before removing it; all files are deleted afterwards.

title: On device, and making room
description: An 'On device' view (also the ON DEVICE filter) listing what is downloaded with size and last played, total used and free per volume, and 'Make room': pick games to delete, largest or least recently played first; never deletes a game whose saves are not uploaded.
acceptance: Deletion goes through the existing uninstall path and refuses when the save queue holds that game (test).
Sizes and free space match `df` and `du` on the fixture (test).

Device check `storage.makeroom`: with three small ROMs in the test home, Make room removes the chosen ones, free space rises by their size (from `df`), and a game with a pending save upload (fake RomM stopped) is refused.

title: Dead rows and wrongly merged games
description: Hide or flag rows RomM marks `missing_from_fs`, and never fold differently named games together just because they share an IGDB (or other provider) id, so stale rows cannot hide real games and sequels are not swallowed.
acceptance: Tests reproduce the Argosy fork's cases (a stale missing row hiding the real game; a sequel sharing a match) and show both fixed.

title: Multi-disc assembly that cannot collide
description: Assemble multi-disc games from `files[]` (not from siblings), write the client's own playlist in a folder whose name does not contain '.m3u' (PCSX ReARMed reads such paths as playlists), ignore any server .m3u, and keep generic track names from overwriting each other.
acceptance: Tests with the fixture's 16-folder PS1 and 6-folder GameCube shapes and a GDI with generic track names.
The playlist path never contains '.m3u' as a folder segment (test).

title: Resumable downloads for folder and zip games
description: Download multi-file games file by file (`?file_ids=` or `/files/content/`), verifying each against `files[].md5_hash` or `sha1_hash`, so every file resumes on its own; use the Range-cached zip only where per-file is impossible.
acceptance: test:romm interrupts a multi-file download mid-file and resumes it without refetching finished files.
A hash mismatch refetches only that file and reports it once.

title: PSP DLC installed for you
description: For PSP rows with `.EDAT` extras, install the DLC into PPSSPP's memory stick `PSP/GAME/<region title id>/` (the folder name must carry the game's own region title id), and remove it with the game.
acceptance: Title id comes from the ISO's PARAM.SFO (parser tests on fixtures); placement and removal are tested.

Device check `psp.dlc`: for the smallest PSP row with `.EDAT` extras, Galleon reads the title id from PARAM.SFO with a capped Range read, places only the DLC files in the PPSSPP sandbox's `PSP/GAME/<title id>/`, and removes them with the game.

title: Per-game PS2 settings applied at launch
description: Apply known per-game ARMSX2 settings (for example blending level 4 for Final Fantasy X; 3 for Metal Gear Solid 2, Jak 1 and 3, Ratchet & Clank 3) through ARMSX2's per-game settings files, which the Android launcher could never pass, without touching the user's global settings.
acceptance: Per-game files are written under ARMSX2's game settings folder keyed by serial/CRC, from a data table with tests.
Device check `armsx2.pergame`: the per-game settings files for the table's serials are written where the Nova's ARMSX2 build reads them (in its sandbox), and the game page lists them (screenshot).

title: Multi-disc PlayStation games play through
description: End to end: a 2-disc PS1 game downloads, launches with its playlist and swaps discs in DuckStation or RetroArch (Beetle PSX HW with PGXP offered as the RetroArch option).
acceptance: Device check `multidisc.playlist`: a two-disc homebrew playlist starts in the sandboxed RetroArch, and the 'next disc' network command switches discs (RetroArch's log shows disc 2).

title: Jellyfin 'Watch' surface (optional)
description: A Watch screen in the fork's design for a Jellyfin server the user adds (address and sign-in kept like the RomM token): continue watching, libraries, play fullscreen with the pad. Off until configured.
acceptance: Tested against a Dockerized Jellyfin with a public-domain clip in CI.
Acceptance session: add your Jellyfin server in Settings, open Watch and play something with sound. Skip this item if you do not use Jellyfin.

title: RomM music, where the server has it
description: If the heartbeat version supports RomM's music API, offer the game soundtrack player; otherwise hide it. Gate by capability, not by guess.
acceptance: Capability check against the 5.2.0 and 5.3.1 schemas in `schema/` decides availability (test).
With music available on the fixture server, a track plays (test:app).

title: Updates that can be undone
